points.title: The subject of todayʼs discourse is “The Supreme Aesthetic Science and the Cult of Devotio
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: The subject of todayʼs discourse is “The Supreme Aesthetic Science and the Cult of Devotion”. What is aesthetic science?
summary: The subject of todayʼs discourse is “The Supreme Aesthetic Science and the Cult of Devotion”. What is aesthetic science? Prehistoric humans used to eat, used to
points.body: The subject of todayʼs discourse is “The Supreme Aesthetic Science and the Cult of Devotion”. What is aesthetic science? Prehistoric humans used to eat, used to walk, used to take bath, used to do so many things. Humans of today also do these things and so long as humans are on this earth they will do the same. It is hoped that humans will live on this globe for many more days to come. Afterwards, when the environment will become uncongenial the human race will cease to exist here. Humans will then live on other stars, other planets. Today where there are no humans there will be in the future, and they will disappear from where they are to day. Collectively the human race will not come to an end.

points.title: Whatever were the daily habits of human beings, whatever they did routinely in pleasure an
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Whatever were the daily habits of human beings, whatever they did routinely in pleasure and pain, are the same today as
summary: Whatever were the daily habits of human beings, whatever they did routinely in pleasure and pain, are the same today as they were in the past. When happy, peopl
points.body: Whatever were the daily habits of human beings, whatever they did routinely in pleasure and pain, are the same today as they were in the past. When happy, people eat in pleasure, and when they feel sad, they may leave food in pain. There is a difference, however, between the cave-dwellers and the aboriginal human beings of the prehistoric period, and present day human beings. Human beings have brought more subtle beauty into the daily tasks and habitual behaviour, which they used to do in a crude way. Before eating, prehistoric human beings did not wash their hands, and they used both hands to eat. Today, we wash our hands, and use the right hand, or a spoon and fork. We enjoy eating in a more subtle fashion. Our sense of beauty is also part of our enjoyment of subtlety. We wear clothes which we feel make us look attractive, not those which we feel make us look odd. In prehistoric times, human beings did not wear clothes. The habit of wearing clothes came into vogue in later times. Various styles of decoration and make-up of the body also have come into vogue over the different ages of human development. Human beings of the past used to dance and jump in joy. Today we also dance and jump, but there is a a definite procedure in our movement; we dance with definite process. The common procedure of the dance of olden days was called “folk dance.” When more finesse was incorporated into dance, it became known as “classical dance”. This very movement from crude to subtle, from ugliness to beauty, from imperfection to perfection is the first stage of aesthetic science.

points.title: Now, what is external change? It is the intro-external projection of the psychic state. Th
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Now, what is external change? It is the intro-external projection of the psychic state. Then, is the introexternal proje
summary: Now, what is external change? It is the intro-external projection of the psychic state. Then, is the introexternal projection of mind all-in-all in aesthetic sc
points.body: Now, what is external change? It is the intro-external projection of the psychic state. Then, is the introexternal projection of mind all-in-all in aesthetic science? No. New likings may occur in the human mental sphere, and new likings do occur in our emotions, in our feelings, also. Though our internal projections are stronger than the external ones. They are not purely internal, they are influenced by extro-internal projections. Human beings started to think in more subtle ways, so their external expressions became more subtle and more beautiful. They also started to want to see beauty, not ugliness or bitterness, in their external surroundings, in the mundane objects of their daily world. This search for beauty, this effort to attain perfection, gave birth to dharma, because when human beings did not get happiness from crude objects, they started moving towards the Subtle one. Human beings today are not satisfied to watch silent movies. They want to see audiovisual films, because these are more subtle; they give more pleasure to the mind.

points.title: Therefore, it is the duty of every person to perform dharma sádhaná. Human beings are ma
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Therefore, it is the duty of every person to perform dharma sádhaná. Human beings are marching along the path of aesth
summary: Therefore, it is the duty of every person to perform dharma sádhaná. Human beings are marching along the path of aesthetic science. Parama Puruśa is describe
points.body: Therefore, it is the duty of every person to perform dharma sádhaná. Human beings are marching along the path of aesthetic science. Parama Puruśa is described as “Truth, Consciousness and Beauty” (Satyam, Shivam, Sundaram). Human beings are fascinated by His grandeur, His non-attachment, and by His beauty too.

points.title: One who charms everybody, who attracts everybody, is called “Krśńa” in the shástras, th
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: One who charms everybody, who attracts everybody, is called “Krśńa” in the shástras, the scriptures. Krśńa means on
summary: One who charms everybody, who attracts everybody, is called “Krśńa” in the shástras, the scriptures. Krśńa means one who attracts all towards Himself. This
points.body: One who charms everybody, who attracts everybody, is called “Krśńa” in the shástras, the scriptures. Krśńa means one who attracts all towards Himself. This is one explanation of the word, Krśńa also means “black” or “dark colour”. When there is black amongst other colours, the eyes are automatically attracted to the black. So human beings are automatically attracted to the Supreme Entity, to Krśńa. They cannot check this attraction. Even if one tries not to be attracted, one will be.

points.title: It is due to the attraction of aesthetic science that we move from imperfection to subtlet
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: It is due to the attraction of aesthetic science that we move from imperfection to subtlety. Why do we move towards the
summary: It is due to the attraction of aesthetic science that we move from imperfection to subtlety. Why do we move towards the Subtlest Entity? The reason is, we want
points.body: It is due to the attraction of aesthetic science that we move from imperfection to subtlety. Why do we move towards the Subtlest Entity? The reason is, we want to experience joy or pleasure. The stage when we lose ourselves in ecstatic bliss, we merge in the Supreme Entity, is called supra-aesthetic science (atinandana vijiṋána). It is also known as sammohana vijiṋána, that is, as long as we are enjoying that ecstasy, we feel it is very charming. The sport (liilá) of Parama Puruśa is very beautiful. We are moving towards Him. We do not mind the obstructions. We will go on moving. The stage of movement is the stage of aesthetic science. The stage of merger, when we have lost ourselves in the Supreme, when we have no desire for anything else, is the stage of supra-aesthetic science (mohana vijiṋána).

points.title: Now according to the devotional scriptures (bhakti-shástras), the first stage of this aes
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Now according to the devotional scriptures (bhakti-shástras), the first stage of this aesthetic science (nandana vijiṋ
summary: Now according to the devotional scriptures (bhakti-shástras), the first stage of this aesthetic science (nandana vijiṋána) is called rágánugá bhakti. Peop
points.body: Now according to the devotional scriptures (bhakti-shástras), the first stage of this aesthetic science (nandana vijiṋána) is called rágánugá bhakti. People may ask, when was this aesthetic science, knowingly or unknowingly, established in ancient times? Is the bhakti shástra [devotional scripture] as old as the cult of devotion (bhakti yoga)? The answer is “Yes, certainly”. Some people say, the cult of devotion is recent. They are not right. The word bhakti is used in the Vedas also. Yasya Devá pará bhaktih yathá deve tathá gurao, that is, only those who have devotion (bhakti) in guru and Deva [God], can attain the goal. Thus the word bhakti is used. So the word bhakti is not recent. Some people say that the Sufism of Persia (Pháras) took the form of bhakti in India. It is not correct. Bhakti shástra, that is, Sufism, was in India, it was also in Persia, it was everywhere in the world. Where there is the human heart there is bhakti, there was bhakti and there will be bhakti. Bhakti is fully established in Tantra and yoga.

points.title: By taking the ideation of Paramátmá [Supreme Subjectivity], the human mind becomes as va
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: By taking the ideation of Paramátmá [Supreme Subjectivity], the human mind becomes as vast as Paramátmá Himself. It
summary: By taking the ideation of Paramátmá [Supreme Subjectivity], the human mind becomes as vast as Paramátmá Himself. It is the characteristic of the mind to tak
points.body: By taking the ideation of Paramátmá [Supreme Subjectivity], the human mind becomes as vast as Paramátmá Himself. It is the characteristic of the mind to take the form of the object of its ideation. It is one of the characteristics of Paramátmá also that whosoever takes His ideation becomes like Him. Everything, such as water, fire, oxygen, nitrogen, etc., has its own characteristic. So the characteristic of Parama Puruśa [Supreme Entity] is that whosoever takes His ideation, become as vast as Him by His Grace. Brhatvadá Brahma brḿhańatvád Brahma. The word Brahma means “very great.” Is He only great? No, He is great Himself, and can make others great; so He is called Brahma. When, by taking His ideation, the human mind becomes like that of Parama Puruśa, it is called savikalpa samádhi” [trance of qualified absorption in Supreme Consciousness]. It becomes one with Him, it merges in Him. Now, after it becomes great, how is it possible to merge this mind in Parama Puruśa? It is only possible by leaving aside all else, then one remains constantly in His ideation.

points.title: What is love? It is the expressed form of devotion. Only one who has love for Parama Purus
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: What is love? It is the expressed form of devotion. Only one who has love for Parama Puruśa can take His ideation. Love
summary: What is love? It is the expressed form of devotion. Only one who has love for Parama Puruśa can take His ideation. Love is the expressed form of devotion. When
points.body: What is love? It is the expressed form of devotion. Only one who has love for Parama Puruśa can take His ideation. Love is the expressed form of devotion. When does this expressed form occur? When it has its root or seed, only then it can occur. When there is seed, only then it will sprout. That seed is devotion. So, only that one can make oneself great, only that one can take the correct ideation of Parama Puruśa, who has the seed of devotion within. Let us see it from another view point. If one, after transforming mind into a point, without making it vast, merges it into Parama Puruśa, surrenders it to Parama Puruśa, then, in that case, individual mind does not exist. Then what happens? Mind merges with Parama Puruśa; there remains only Paramátma [Supreme Subjectivity] and not the mind. This is called nirvikalpa samádhi. In savikalpa samádhi the mind enjoys bliss because of its greatness. That bliss is called liilánanda [bliss of the divine play]. When the mind is given to Parama Puruśa, it is surrendered unto Him, in that condition the bliss or supra-mundane ecstasy is called nityánanda [eternal, transcendental bliss]. So devotion is essential to get nityánanda or liilánanda (the bliss of His sport or liilá).

points.title: How can you surrender the self without bhakti, or devotion? Therefore from ancient times a
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: How can you surrender the self without bhakti, or devotion? Therefore from ancient times aesthetic science existed in th
summary: How can you surrender the self without bhakti, or devotion? Therefore from ancient times aesthetic science existed in the human mind and there was the cult of d
points.body: How can you surrender the self without bhakti, or devotion? Therefore from ancient times aesthetic science existed in the human mind and there was the cult of devotion. While one remains in aesthetic science, one does not get entry into the supra-aesthetic science. One feels, “I am serving Parama Puruśa, I like Him, because I get pleasure in serving Him, by taking His ideation I get joy.” If you ask artists or architects as to why they are busy with their art, they will say, “We get pleasure from it.” This is aesthetic science. A poet composes a poem because he or she gets pleasure.

points.body: Parents love their child very much. Do they love for the sake of their child? No they love their child because they get pleasure for themselves. If their child turns into a vagabond, if he or she becomes cruel, then he or she does not utter even the parents’ names, then they do not get pleasure. A person likes everything of this world but not for the sake of these things. One loves the world, one lives with this world because one gets pleasure, that is why one loves it. You see, if one gets great trouble in this world even for a single moment one says, “O Yamarája (God of Death), where are you? Come on, now, I donʼt want to live.” After that if one gets attracted towards this world after two or three minutes, one says, “No Yamarája, no, you donʼt come now.” So this is the first phase of aesthetic science.

points.body: After that what happens? By taking the ideation of Parama Puruśa, when the quantity of pleasure increases, a person loses the self first. What happens when he or she is lost? He or she feels “I take the ideation of Parama Puruśa not for my sake, not for me. I love Parama Puruśa so that he may get pleasure because of my love, I wish to give Him pleasure. I may or may not get it.” When this stage is attained, this is called rágátmiká bhakti. In this stage one feels, “I love Parama Puruśa, I do not care whether He loves me or lot, He likes me or not, but I like Him”. This is rágátmiká bhakti. When this rágátmiká bhakti is attained, in that stage one is also called gopa” as described in scriptures (shástras):

points.body: Gopa here does not mean a cowherd, or the caretaker of cows. Gopáyate means “to give pleasure” – Gopáyate yah sah gopah. One whose nature is to give pleasure to Parama Puruśa or Paramátmá is a gopa. When rágátmiká bhakti is attained, when one is established in rágátmiká bhakti from rágánugá, one enters the arena of mohana vijiṋána [supra-aesthetic science]. At that stage one is fascinated, one is charmed, and in that state, art, architecture, all come to an end; oneʼs verbosity stops, one becomes mute. This is rágátmiká bhakti. So long as human beings are in the sphere of rágánugá bhakti they are in domestic life; they create arts, architecture, literature, painting, etc. and get pleasure in them. They are within the scope of aesthetic science (nandana vijiṋána). And what happens when they are established in supra-aesthetic science (atinandan vijiṋána)? All their worldly music is finished. All the rágas and rágińiis and the art of dancing, whatever they be, they come to an end. In that condition, there remains only an ecstatic state (bhávibhora). The music of that state is called kiirtana.

points.title: Therefore, it is the scriptural direction not to sing any song after kiirtana, because oth

summary: Therefore, it is the scriptural direction not to sing any song after kiirtana, because other music is within the scope of aesthetic science and kiirtana comes w
points.body: Therefore, it is the scriptural direction not to sing any song after kiirtana, because other music is within the scope of aesthetic science and kiirtana comes within the scope of mohana vijiṋána. This mohana vijiṋána is the supra-aesthetic science. Bhaktitattva [essence of devotion] is supra-aesthetic. Therefore, kiirtana is, in its essential form, with devotion, it is in the form of ota [individual] and prota [collective]. So in the life of a spiritual practitioner (sádhaka), in the life of a devotee (bhakta), kiirtana is most essential. In mentioning the subject of discourse, I said bhakti yoga. In English I said “cult”, because there is no word for yoga in English, so I said “cult”, but actually devotion (bhakti) is not a cult. Devotion is the terminating point, devotion is the desideratum, devotion is not a path. Some people say, “Our path is the path of spiritual practice (sádhaná).” Devotion is the goal. When devotion is established, everything is established, there remains nothing. To get established in devotion you do something, you do something else. Hence, devotion is not the path, devotion is the goal. Devotion and Paramátmá [Cosmic Self] go together. Therefore the seat of Paramátmá is in the hearts of those who are established in devotion, who are devotees. When you are established in devotion, you get Paramátmá too. Then you will experience yourselves that Paramátmá is seated in your heart, you will not have to go elsewhere in search of Him. It is the dictum of bhágavata shástra.

points.body: Then comes shrii, meaning “charm”, or “attraction”. People will be attracted towards Him. Shrii means “charm”, “fascination”. The acoustic root (biija mantra) in Sanskrit is talavya [palatal] sha, which means the mutative principle, the mutative effulgence, and ra means energy – light, magnetism, electricity – all forms of energy. Actually energy is one. So where mutative charm and energy are there it is sha and ra, that is, shra, and the feminine gender is Shrii. That is why there has been an ancient custom in India to prefix “Shrii” before the name of persons. So He possesses shrii in complete form.

points.body: So Bhagaván says to Narada (nárada means that power of Parama Puruśa by which devotion germinates in the hearts of living beings), “Oh, Narada, people say that I live in Vaekúńtha, which is somewhere in the sky. No, I donʼt live there.” The meaning of the kuńthá word in vaekúńtha is “without complexes”. Vigata kuńt́ha – here there are no complexes. So where there is no complex, either inferiority or superiority, no fear complex, etc., it is the stage of vigata kuńt́ha. It is a stage without any complexes. It is vaekuńt́ha. So when there is no complex in the mind, no contraction in the mind, then only will one feel Parama Puruśa or His existence in oneʼs heart. That is why it is called vaekuńt́ha. Now what is the dictum here? It is “I do not reside in Vaekuńt́ha or any [heaven in the] sky, neither do I reside in the hearts of yogis” – Yogińám hradaye na ca. Here yogi means hat́ha yogi, one who suspends his mental propensities forcibly. When the propensities have been suspended, there will be no emanation of any propensity; there will not be any sentiment or any ideal. So when the flow has been checked, what will Parama Puruśa do by sitting there? Sitting there means He Himself has remained in a suspended form. There will not be any expression. Parama Puruśa wants to make the world dance. Everybody will be dancing with His vibrations and in His tune. Parama Puruśa will be enjoying with all. Does He not want this? Why should He live in the dry heart of a yogi? He would like a sweet, loving heart – Sarasa hrdaya. He will not like the desert. He would like fertile land. So, the heart of a devotee is like the fertile land.

points.body: That is why Parama Puruśa says, Madbhaktá yatra gáyante, that is, “Wherever my devotees perform kiirtana in full swing, at once I reach there.” You may say that Parama Puruśa is omnipresent. Now, Parama Puruśa is omnipotent, He is also omniscient, it is a fact; but there is a hub of that omniscience, there is a hub of those premonitions and post-monitions of all expressions. A central point is there. Parama Puruśa is omnipresent, but He has a Nucleus (Cakranábhi). Parama Puruśa will place that Nucleus wherever He likes. He will take it wherever He likes. Parama Puruśa says, “When my devotees sit single-minded for kiirtana (Ananyor mamáta Viśńormamatá – “exclusive devotion to the Supreme Entity to the exclusion of all others”), I at once take myself there. This is what I do.”

Now I say, if you want to be established in dharma sádhaná, then do not forget in any case the importance of kiirtana, the greatness of kiirtana, and also the greatness of devotion. Always remember that devotion begins with aesthetic science; and the ultimate domain [of aesthetic science] ends where supra-aesthetic science (mohana vijiṋána) begins.

points.body: Regarding the first duty of a devotee it has been said, Trńádapi suniicena. Trńá means “grass”. Even though grass is one of the most beautiful things on this Earth, it remains one of the lowliest. Yet without it millions of animals would not have been able to sustain their lives. If there is anything which properly represents the state of egolessness, it is grass. Humans should always be free from ego, free from any superiority complex. Each complex, be it fear, defeatist, superiority or inferiority complex is a type of psychic disease. Complexes originate in a certain environment and in due course become completely overpowering. They are most detrimental to human progress. A person seeking all-round welfare should not allow any complex to take root in the mind.

points.body: All are the progeny of Parama Puruśa. Even so, some people think that because they are endowed with less intellect, knowledge, financial capacity or physical strength than others, they are inferior. Such an inferiority complex contracts their minds and retards their progress. It must be overcome.

points.title: The fear complex is even more harmful than the inferiority complex. People suffer from it,

summary: The fear complex is even more harmful than the inferiority complex. People suffer from it, often without reason, when they encounter something more powerful tha
points.body: The fear complex is even more harmful than the inferiority complex. People suffer from it, often without reason, when they encounter something more powerful than themselves. For example, thinking that a ghost is nearby, a man becomes terrified – his mind contracts and he becomes paralysed. Were he to take a few steps forward he would discover that the ghost does not exist at all. Fear, in most cases is baseless. If one marches on with courage, one finds that there was no reason to be so afraid.

points.body: I had a certain acquaintance whose garden was quite large. One night his wife thought she saw a ghost in a corner of the garden. In Bihar, a female ghost is called cuŕeil in Hindi. At the sight of the imagined ghost she cried out in fear, and fainted. She never regained consciousness and died some time later. The next night the same gentleman came out of his house at the same time. He also thought he saw the ghost. “Why should people have to die one after the other in this way?” he thought. Stepping forward to strike at the imaginary ghost with a stick, he suddenly saw that it was nothing but a bush which, in the moonlight, looked just like a human being. His wife had died for nothing, terrified by the deceptive image of a bush. Most so-called ghosts are like this. Towards the end of the rainy season rotting vegetation often gives out a gas, called marsh gas or will-o’-the-wisp, which bursts into flame when it comes in contact with oxygen. This burning gas may easily be taken to be a ghost. This is how a fear complex can develop.

points.body: The defeatist complex also strikes deep in the human mind. “How will I possibly be able to do the work? How will I be able to fight against such heavy odds? How will I be able to do my job properly?” Because people think like this before they act, they are unable to do their work properly. The defeatist complex weakens their minds. Had they been bolder they would have been more successful.

points.body: The most dangerous complex in the spiritual sphere is the superiority complex. It occurs when one feels oneself to be greater than others in knowledge, intellect, wisdom, and so on, and eventually leads to oneʼs downfall. On the spiritual path, the most essential thing is to withdraw the mind from all kinds of objects, concentrate it on one point, and finally surrender it to Parama Puruśa. But those suffering from a superiority complex, and thus an over-inflated ego, find it impossible to withdraw the mind from its objects and, to their frustration, find that the mind easily slips away from its point of concentration. They will never be able to surrender such a mind to Parama Puruśa. These people fail to realize that the more the ego is inflated, the more the mind loses its weight, just as the more rice is puffed, the lighter it becomes – inside is nothing but air. To prevent this from happening, the following advice has been given: Trńádapi suniicena. Always remember that you should never give any indulgence to any superiority complex under any circumstances. That would be most harmful; it would be the greatest foolishness on your part.

points.body: Tároriva sahiśńuńá. Those who overreact at the least provocation lose their power of judgement. Oneʼs internal power is determined by the degree of control one has over oneʼs nerve cells. A person who cannot tolerate even a single provocative word obviously has no control over the nerves. His enemies can take full advantage of him by easily provoking him. He will never be able to do anything great because his self-confidence is easily shattered. One must always be in control of oneʼs nerve fibres and for that one must develop the power of tolerance. It is highly gratifying to note that many of our members were able to properly maintain control over their nerve cells and fibres while in prison during the period of Emergency [from June 1975 to March 1977 the Government of India proclaimed a State of Emergency and put hundreds of innocent citizens behind bars], even under the pressure of circumstances. That period was very painful and it certainly seemed many a time that things were getting beyond our endurance. To many it actually reached that stage and yet, even when faced with such tremendous circumstantial pressure, they tolerated immense hardship and, as a result, have now acquired the capacity of endurance. This is a fact. Everything has two sides – good and bad. Hence it is said, Tároriva sahiśńuńá [“with the power of endurance of a tree”].

points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ. Human beings neglect many things in this world without any plausible reason. They forget that P
summary: Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ. Human beings neglect many things in this world without any plausible reason. They forget that Parama Puruśa resides in every object, e
points.body: Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ. Human beings neglect many things in this world without any plausible reason. They forget that Parama Puruśa resides in every object, even the most neglected one. They fail to look at the world with proper social benevolence. Suppose a pig is writhing in pain. The onlookers casually say, “Well, itʼs only a pig – let it die,” and thus neglect Parama Puruśa in the form of a pig. Such an error will result in their overall progress being retarded. One should not detest anything, as everything is a manifestation of Parama Puruśa. Parama Puruśa cannot hate anyone or anything in this world – how can He, all are His manifestations – so on what grounds can humans hate anyone or anything? If one hates His manifestation it means that one hates Parama Puruśa Himself. Let no human being be so arrogant. It has been said, Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ – “respect the disrespected.” Those who are disrespected and rejected by society should also be recognized by us as manifestations of Parama Puruśa. We must respect them with due honour as Parama Puruśa has chosen to manifest them in that particular way. We should always be very courteous to them. Hence the third duty of a devotee is to respect those people whom no one respects. We must approach those who are unloved, ridiculed, and in need of affection, and tell them we care for them. By honouring them and restoring their dignity we will make them happy; their minds will become filled with joy.

points.body: It is not with oneʼs own strength and intellect that one does great things in life, but with the strength and intellect given by Parama Puruśa. Most of the credit for oneʼs great actions should therefore go to Him. Someone who donates 100 million rupees to a worthy cause will be called a philanthropist. But the question is, who actually owns the money? In fact it is Parama Puruśaʼs money which happens to come in the possession of that so-called philanthropist. The main credit should therefore go to Parama Puruśa and the secondary credit to the donor whom Parama Puruśa was kind enough to use as a medium. That is why, if anyone is to be praised in this world, if anyoneʼs virtues are to be extolled loudly through kiirtana, it should be Parama Puruśa. Kiirtana means to utter good words aloud; not mentally, nor in a whisper, but loud enough for everyone to hear. It is never done secretly, but always openly. There is no place in a devoteeʼs life for hypocrisy – the devoteeʼs thoughts, words and actions will never be contradictory. These simple and straightforward people will say what they think and do what they say. So devotees will openly sing praises to Parama Puruśa. Kiirtana means, as I said a little earlier, to sing the Lordʼs glory in a loud voice.

points.title: Kiirtaniiyah sadá Harih. What is the meaning of “Hari”? Philosophy says that this univers

summary: Kiirtaniiyah sadá Harih. What is the meaning of “Hari”? Philosophy says that this universe is the playground of Hari and Hara. Hari maintains this universe and
points.body: Kiirtaniiyah sadá Harih. What is the meaning of “Hari”? Philosophy says that this universe is the playground of Hari and Hara. Hari maintains this universe and Hara destroys it. What form does this destruction take? He withdraws the objects of the world into Himself and projects them again in a newer form. Suppose you create an image of a wicked demon in your mind but decide that it is too dreadful. You can easily annihilate it and create an image of an honest person in its place. You can easily create and destroy images in your mind – you are doing this all the time. In the same way, Parama Puruśa withdraws an image or an idea into Himself and the very next moment sends another image or idea back into the universe. It is not destruction or dreadful annihilation as people are generally prone to believe, but withdrawal followed by the creation of the same image in a newer way invested with greater capacity. Does Hari send back a person who has been liberated from all sorts of past saḿskáras by dint of sádhaná? No, a person who attains permanent liberation is assimilated into Him. “Hari” here means Parama Puruśa. The entity which is instrumental for the withdrawal of everything is called “Hara”, and the entity responsible for the creation of unit beings is called “Hari”. This is the fundamental difference between Hari and Hara.

summary: Hara is derived from two letters: ha and ra. Ha is the acoustic root of the ethereal factor, and ra the acoustic root of energy. So the entity who, by virtue of
points.body: Hara is derived from two letters: ha and ra. Ha is the acoustic root of the ethereal factor, and ra the acoustic root of energy. So the entity who, by virtue of His tremendous power, withdraws and projects all the five fundamental factors up to the ethereal factor, is called “Hara”.

points.title: What is Hariʼs role? Human beings have been committing numerous crimes and sins for lives
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: What is Hariʼs role? Human beings have been committing numerous crimes and sins for lives together resulting in a huge p
summary: What is Hariʼs role? Human beings have been committing numerous crimes and sins for lives together resulting in a huge pile of sins as high as the Himalayas. If
points.body: What is Hariʼs role? Human beings have been committing numerous crimes and sins for lives together resulting in a huge pile of sins as high as the Himalayas. If they have to carry the full load of those sins, they will surely break their backs; and if they have to atone for them all, they will have to return to this world again and again for at least 20 generations. Now the question arises, why should Hari exist? Why should Parama Puruśa exist if He cannot help individuals? Well, He does render assistance and in that capacity He is called Hari. “Harati pápáni ityarthe harih.” One who steals others sins to lighten their burden and pave the way for their liberation, is called Hari. Why would Hari steal sins? Stealing, after all, is a despicable act. What is stealing? Stealing is taking things which belong to others without their permission. Why should He wish to steal others’ things? It does not seem to be a very wise thing to do. On closer analysis, however, it is seen to be a most commendable act because the main purpose of Hariʼs theft is to lighten the burden of the devotees load; otherwise they will never attain liberation, but will continue to suffer from the reactions of sins for lives together. What does He want? As His devotees have surrendered everything to Him, He would like to relieve them of the burden of their sins. He wishes to say to His devotees, “My dear children, give me all your sins. You wonʼt be able to carry such a heavy load of sins. Remember that you have been committing sins for lives together and it will take you as many as twenty lives to undergo the consequences. So it would be better for you to give me all your sins to free yourself of your burden.”

points.body: It is a fact that Hari loves His devotees very much; so much that perhaps He even loves them more than He loves Himself. So what does He do? He steals the devotees’ sins without them knowing. There is no other option, as the devotees refuse to give Him their sins voluntarily. Devotees may offer delicious dishes or even holy basil leaves, but under no circumstances will they part with their sins. He is compelled to steal their sins when their backs are turned. One who steals others’ sins is called Hari.

When a person does kiirtana, the tongue acts according to the command of the mind, and the ears hear that kiirtana. Under the command of the mind, the motor and sensory organs are activated. At that time, the person loves Parama Puruśa and no one else. If, while doing kiirtana, a spiritual aspirant keeps in mind this truth, the personʼs mind must get absorbed in kiirtana. How can Parama Puruśa remain away from one whose mind becomes absorbed in Him due to love for Him? Even if Parama Puruśa wants to keep Himself away from this bond of love, He cannot. It means that Parama Puruśa cannot remain away without answering the call of His devotees. He does not have that freedom. That is why it is said, Madbhaktá yatra gáyanti tatra tiśt́hámi Nárada.

points.body: So far, no sound that has ever been created has been lost. Even sounds from billions and billions of years ago still reverberate in the mahákásha [vast Cosmic void]. Human beings cannot hear these sounds with their crude ears. But many subtle sounds can be heard through specially-designed instruments. All acoustic expressions of Parama Puruśa are stored in the vast antariikśa [outer space]. If a person does kiirtana regularly, the person will get kiirtana siddhi. After one attains kiirtana siddhi, if the person remains alone, the person will hear the oṋḿkára. This is also a saḿkalpa [resolution] of Parama Puruśa. Spiritual practice can be done alone, but not kiirtana. So you must do kiirtana collectively.

points.body: A sound like t́hak-t́hak – what is this sound? It is the acoustic root of sound produced when one moves wearing wooden sandals. Upon hearing this sound, we understand that someone is moving. (You must have seen wooden sandals. Nowadays wooden sandals are not in vogue.) So if someone is moving wearing wooden sandals, what type of sound is he or she creating? T́hak-t́hak-t́hak. In Sanskrit, T́hak-t́hak karoti ityarthe t́hakkara [“One who makes the sound t́hak-t́ha k is a t́hakkara”]. From Sanskrit, the Bengali word t́hákur has come. The word t́hákur means “one who is moving wearing wooden sandals instead of moving wearing leather shoes”. Even now, in some families, you will find the surname T́hákur [Tagore]. It has the same meaning.

points.title: So a sound is created based on an acoustic root in this manner, and not only in the extern

points.body: So a sound is created based on an acoustic root in this manner, and not only in the external world but also in the psychic world. Take for instance the colour red. This colour must change according to space, time and person. The psychic wave, the internal acoustic root, that this colour will create in [the minds of] the people of Bengal will not be just like that in the case of the people of Arabia. It will be a little different. Climate has some influence. Suppose that someone sees a white colour as very white. He or she sees the colour; that is, the colour comes before his or her eyes. That colour, with the help of the nerve fibres, goes to the nerve cells. From there, it comes within the mind. That is, the mind reflects the colour. You see the white colour even within your mind. Seeing with the eyes will not do; when you see it within your mind, that is real seeing.

summary: When you are seeing, vibrations come in the mind, waves of white colour come. Every wave has a vibration. That vibration arises in the mind. Because of the vibr
points.body: When you are seeing, vibrations come in the mind, waves of white colour come. Every wave has a vibration. That vibration arises in the mind. Because of the vibration, a sound is created. That sound is much like the sound dhav-dhav. That is why in Bengali we say dhavdhave shádá [shádá means “white”]. In Sanskrit, [the root dhav + lá] + the suffix d́a = dhavala. Its meaning is “white”. If one sees the colour red, a sound like t́akt́ak is produced. In Bengali we say t́akt́ake lál [lál means “red”]. All these things stem from the influence of acoustic roots. Different types of acoustic root and mantra sounds emanate, as effects, from different physical and psychic objects.

summary: Now, such a sound is both within and without. You speak through your mouth. Suppose you ask your cousin, “How is Uncle (the cousinʼs father)?” You say this with
points.body: Now, such a sound is both within and without. You speak through your mouth. Suppose you ask your cousin, “How is Uncle (the cousinʼs father)?” You say this with your mouth. But suppose your cousin is not there. You can see your cousin within your mind. You can see the picture of your cousin within your mind. And you ask your cousin within your mind, “How is Uncle?” No one hears this sound. Only you and the cousin within your mind hear it. Now, you have two worlds. One is the external world wherein you may ask your cousin of the external world, with your mouth, how your uncle is. [The other is the world within your mind, wherein] you may ask your cousin of the mind, with your mind, how your uncle is. The meaning of thought is “to speak within the mind”. If, sitting here, you think of some subject, that is actually talking within the mind. “I will go to Agartala tomorrow; I will tell my father and go” – you are actually speaking within your mind.

points.title: So human beings have two worlds – one is the outside world and another is the inside world
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: So human beings have two worlds – one is the outside world and another is the inside world. But, to Parama Puruśa, ther
summary: So human beings have two worlds – one is the outside world and another is the inside world. But, to Parama Puruśa, there is no outside world. The entire Vishva
points.body: So human beings have two worlds – one is the outside world and another is the inside world. But, to Parama Puruśa, there is no outside world. The entire Vishvabrahmáńd́a [Cosmos] is within His mind. Whatever He creates – human beings, cows, sheep, goats, mountains, rivers – He thinks up everything within His mind, just as you thought up your cousin. Nothing is outside Him. Now if your cousin starts dancing the táńd́ava dance, you will see that dance within your mind. Similarly, the humans of the earth do different types of work. Whatever they think or speak, everything happens within the mind of Parama Puruśa. So He comes to know everything. He knows it then and there. And you may think that on ekádashii day, you have eaten a candy secretly, and that no one saw you. But Parama Puruśa has seen that you, hiding here or there, have eaten candy secretly and thought that no one saw you. This is how it happens. You can create an elephant with a bit of clay. But Parama Puruśa creates elephants within His mind. Whatever elephants we see on earth, all those elephants have been created by Parama Puruśa with His mánasadhátu [mind-stuff, mental substance]. Parama Puruśa has built the world. When He creates the world, a movement of His ectoplasmic stuff [mind-stuff, mental substance] takes place. [By creating an object which is psychic for Him, an object of the world] is brought into existence. Because of this creation, a sound is produced. It is similar to the t́hak-t́hak sound created because of movement. We call it t́hakkara, or t́hákur. Similarly, Tur-tur karoti iti turauṋgam; when a horse moves, a tur-tur sound is created. That is why a horse is called turauṋgam.

points.title: When Parama Puruśa creates something, a sound is produced within His mind. In all of His

summary: When Parama Puruśa creates something, a sound is produced within His mind. In all of His mental ectoplasmic stuff, inter-electronic movement [movement of the c
points.body: When Parama Puruśa creates something, a sound is produced within His mind. In all of His mental ectoplasmic stuff, inter-electronic movement [movement of the cittáńu, particles of ectoplasm] is also created. The distance of the inter-electronic stuff [the mutual distance between ectoplasmic particles] increases and decreases. Because of this, a sound is produced. When Parama Puruśa creates something, the sound that is produced within His mind is a-a-a. That is why a is the first letter of the Indo-Aryan alphabetical order. Because a is the seed of creation. When Parama Puruśa creates something, sound is produced. Now see, if the a sound is the biija mantra [acoustic root, literally “seed mantra”] of creation, then a must be a mantra, that is, a biija [seed] mantra.

summary: Similarly, when creatures are created, they have to be protected. Parama Puruśa does everything for their feeding and thriving. This protection and preservatio
points.body: Similarly, when creatures are created, they have to be protected. Parama Puruśa does everything for their feeding and thriving. This protection and preservation has another sound. That sound is u-u-u. U is the acoustic root of preservation. Suppose someone is depriving someone else of his/her right to live; or is depriving some person or some clan of their legal rights; or is conspiring to make someone their slave. That is, suppose someone is opposing the acoustic expression u of Parama Puruśa. Do you understand? Then he/she is an enemy of the human race. Suppose you collect financial resources to take care of your family and society. If someone wants to destroy you through exploitation, sucking your blood, wants to deprive you of all, then he/she goes against u, the acoustic root of Parama Puruśa. The destruction of that person, that sinner, that exploiter is highly desired by Parama Puruśa. So if you fight against such evil forces and exploitative forces, you will surely get the blessing of Parama Puruśa, because such a person is under the curse of God.

points.title: Now comes ma. Ma is the acoustic root of pratyáhára. If you create an elephant within yo

summary: Now comes ma. Ma is the acoustic root of pratyáhára. If you create an elephant within your mind, you cannot keep that elephant in your mind for long. You cann
points.body: Now comes ma. Ma is the acoustic root of pratyáhára. If you create an elephant within your mind, you cannot keep that elephant in your mind for long. You cannot keep the cousin whom you created within your mind for long. [In your mind,] your cousin is standing there. You feed him some Comilla rasogollá. Thereafter, he will slowly fade out of your mind. How long can he remain in your mind? Then your pisimá [fatherʼs sister] may come into your mind. No one will remain for a long time. Parama Puruśa, likewise, creates many things and slowly withdraws them. ( 1 ) This is destruction. Human beings fear this. They think it is death. But for Parama Puruśa, it is different. He created within His mind, preserved within His mind, and, a little later, drew it back within Himself. Generally to human beings, death is frightful. But it is a sweet arrangement to Parama Puruśa. He forms within His mind and merges within His mind. Do you understand that it is a sweet arrangement, not a dreadful one? But for the members of that society, [the dead person] was snatched from among them. All cry in the pain of loss, and it is natural to cry, because they are human beings – it is not unnatural. One who was close to them goes far away. He/she will never return. But if viewed from a wide angle, you will see that someone has left us, but still remains blissfully within the [Cosmic] Mind in which he/she was created. He/she will merge in His mind and live with bliss. We have to explain for peopleʼs minds, and console their minds, using the following words:

summary: So behind every shabda tanmátra, in every expression, there are these acoustic roots –a, á, ka, kha. The first letter of the Indo-Aryan alphabet is a, and the
points.body: So behind every shabda tanmátra, in every expression, there are these acoustic roots –a, á, ka, kha. The first letter of the Indo-Aryan alphabet is a, and the last letter is kśa. Because of this, the collective name of these fifty letters is akśamálá. Its first letter is a, and the last letter is kśa. All acoustic expressions are not only full of sound, but have colour also. Each one has a different colour. All waves have not only sonic expression, they have also expression of colour. Starting from a, there are fifty letters or fifty sounds, and each has its own sound and colour. For this reason, another term for akśamálá is varńamálá; that is, we call the totality of these letters svaravarńa [vowels] and vyaiṋjanvarńa [consonants]. The meaning of varńa is “colour”. There are fifty new sounds side by side with fifty new colours [at the time of creation]. In Latin, you may call this the Causal Matrix. In Sanskrit you may call it mátrká varńa. The meaning of this Causal Matrix is “that from which this world is emanated”. Therefore the fifty varńas are also called Vishvamátá [Mother of the Universe]. But to attain Parama Puruśa, three of them are important. The seed of creation is a, the seed of preservation is u, and the seed of destruction is ma. A + u + ma = om [two more elements are needed in order for it to become oṋm].

points.body: But to be established in the supreme stance of Parama Puruśa, this is not enough. For this, one needs a particular mantra which will be decided according to the saḿskáras of the individual. It is called the Iśt́a mantra. The meaning of Iśt́a is “very dear”. Human beings move ahead with the help of their Iśt́a mantra.

points.body: Here the meaning of mantra is Iś t́a mantra. Now let us see how to pronounce the Iśt́a mantra. Is it within the mind or with the mouth? One should not pronounce it with the mouth, because, if one does, it is a physical expression. Whereas if you pronounce within the mind, it is a psychic expression. These [mantras] create waves in the realm of the mind. The waves emanated in the realm of the mind can easily work in the spiritual realm. Work that is done in the physical realm cannot as easily be effective in the spiritual realm. Because of this, if one keeps oneʼs Iśt́a mantra within oneʼs mind, greater results can be obtained. summary: Now what is kiirtana? Kiirtana is one type of mantra, that is, a siddha mantra. A siddha mantra is that by which jaevii shakti can be transformed into Daevii sh
points.body: Now what is kiirtana? Kiirtana is one type of mantra, that is, a siddha mantra. A siddha mantra is that by which jaevii shakti can be transformed into Daevii shakti ( 2 ) – other mantras will not work. So what is kiirtana? Kiirtana is goading all emotions of the heart, all feelings of the heart towards Parama Puruśa. Here, feeling is greater than sound. A feeling, a vibration, comes into oneʼs heart if one performs kiirtana continuously for some time. When this vibration reaches very close to the Universal Nucleus, then human beings very easily enjoy bliss. The big advantage of coming close to the Universal Nucleus is this: Parama Puruśa has a position. That is, He operates everywhere, but the Universal Nucleus (an aspect of Parama Puruśa) has a nuclear existence, a particular point. This particular point comes within the kiirtanamańd́alii [group of devotees performing kiirtana]. For this reason, the value of kiirtana is very great in the life of every human being. summary: Náhaḿ tiśt́hámi Vaekuńt́he yogináḿ hrdaye na ca. A yogi suspends all his/her propensities and makes the heart expressionless and stops all its expression
points.body: Náhaḿ tiśt́hámi Vaekuńt́he yogináḿ hrdaye na ca. A yogi suspends all his/her propensities and makes the heart expressionless and stops all its expressions. Why does Bhagaván [the Lord] not place His nucleus there? The answer is that Parama Puruśa moves forward in dance postures in the expressed waves of the Vishvabrahmáńd́a [this elliptical Cosmos] – in rhythm, sweetness, colour, and beyond colour. But no ideation gets expressed from the suspended hearts of yogis. A yogi is just sitting – his/her body has become akin to wood. Even the beating of the heart has stopped. What would be the profit [for Parama Puruśa] in living in that heart? No vibration will be emanated from there in all directions. It will remain blocked there. This is just like sowing seeds on stone. So, where does He in fact reside?

For this reason, you should keep in mind that your own Iśt́a mantra has much value on the sádhanámárga [path of spiritual practice], and that similarly, the value of kiirtana is inestimable in transforming your own heartʼs expressions into vishvatiita vibrations [vibrations transcending the universe]. Always keep this thought in mind as you observe all the rules of your individual daily life.

summary: According to scripture, one name for Parama Puruśa is Viśńu. The word is derived from the Sanskrit root verb viś (“to enter”). The word viśńu means “expan
points.body: According to scripture, one name for Parama Puruśa is Viśńu. The word is derived from the Sanskrit root verb viś (“to enter”). The word viśńu means “expansive” – that is, “one who pervades every entity”. Because of this infinite, limitless, unbroken and omnipresent entity, other objects remain alive. As fish cannot live without water, living beings cannot survive, and nothing can exist, without Parama Puruśa. In fact, everything exists because He exists. But it is also a fact that in some places He is visible, elsewhere invisible.

points.title: Parama Puruśa does not live in Vaekuńt́ha, nor does He live in the hearts of yogis. This
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Parama Puruśa does not live in Vaekuńt́ha, nor does He live in the hearts of yogis. This statement seems confusing. Ac
summary: Parama Puruśa does not live in Vaekuńt́ha, nor does He live in the hearts of yogis. This statement seems confusing. According to the Puranas, Vaekuńt́ha is t
points.body: Parama Puruśa does not live in Vaekuńt́ha, nor does He live in the hearts of yogis. This statement seems confusing. According to the Puranas, Vaekuńt́ha is the highest location. He should have resided there. Yet He says He does not reside there. Vaekuńt́ha or Goloka, that is, the so-called Vaekuńt́ha or Goloka, is not a specific place. But in the sense of Vigata kuńt́ha yasmin, vaekuńt́ha does have meaning. Kuńt́ha means “contraction”. Thus “Vaekuńt́ha” means the heart of a devotee. Remembering Parama Puruśa, people become rapt in dance, song, smiles and tears. Not an iota of shame or diffidence, contraction or crudeness, remains. If we accept this meaning of the word vaekuńt́ha, Parama Puruśa must reside there. Throughout the three worlds, there is no specific geographical place named Vaekuńt́ha. To search for Parama Puruśa, it is not necessary to go to a place called Vaekuńt́ha.

points.title: The current civilization has a fake element, an artificiality. Here one has to express his
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: The current civilization has a fake element, an artificiality. Here one has to express his/her joy and sorrow, laughter
summary: The current civilization has a fake element, an artificiality. Here one has to express his/her joy and sorrow, laughter and tears, shame and diffidence, in a co
points.body: The current civilization has a fake element, an artificiality. Here one has to express his/her joy and sorrow, laughter and tears, shame and diffidence, in a controlled way, and not spontaneously. So the hearts of all human beings are not vaekuńt́ha. What is the matter in the case of yogis? Yogashcittavrttinirodhah. The process of yoga tends to stop the expression of all propensities. In this sense the doors of the hearts of all yogis are closed. How can Parama Puruśa enter such hearts? That is why He says, yogináḿ hrdaye na ca. A heart without love for Parama Puruśa is dried up. So Parama Puruśa does not reside in such a hard, dry place. The most beloved abode of Parama Puruśa is the heart of a devotee. Dancing and singing, a devotee smilingly calls his/her loving Hari inside such a heart. And there is no scope for shame or diffidence where there is no existence of any third entity except bhakta and Bhagaván [the devotee and the Lord].

points.title: Three types of devotee are found. One type of devotee thinks – Parama Puruśa belongs to a
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Three types of devotee are found. One type of devotee thinks – Parama Puruśa belongs to all, and He is omnipresent. And
summary: Three types of devotee are found. One type of devotee thinks – Parama Puruśa belongs to all, and He is omnipresent. And because I am one among these “all” and
points.body: Three types of devotee are found. One type of devotee thinks – Parama Puruśa belongs to all, and He is omnipresent. And because I am one among these “all” and I am in the universe, Parama Puruśa is mine too. These devotees are not great ones. We see another type of devotee also. They say, “Bhagaván is mine. But He belongs to everyone, at the same time.” This is not an elevated type of devotion either. Then there is another type of devotee. They say, “Parama Puruśa is mine alone. He is my individual property. I do not want to share this property with anyone.” ( 1 ) We are to remember one thing. Vaekuńt́ha does not exist inside pundits and books. Iishvara [God as the Controller] does not reside there.

points.title: Devotees have a separate world. All devotees of the universe find a place there. Between t
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Devotees have a separate world. All devotees of the universe find a place there. Between them, there is no dividing line
summary: Devotees have a separate world. All devotees of the universe find a place there. Between them, there is no dividing line, no artificial barrier. That world is a
points.body: Devotees have a separate world. All devotees of the universe find a place there. Between them, there is no dividing line, no artificial barrier. That world is above differences in caste, lineage, mental colour, or country. Its name is Hariparimańd́ala [“circle of devotees around the Lord who removes sins”]. Let everybody try to be a member of that Hariparimańd́ala. Parama Puruśa is the central jewel of that Hariparimańd́ala. In His sweet ideational flow, everyone laughs, cries, dances, and sings. In that ocean of ideation or ocean of rasa [flow], the rásaliilá ( 2 ) of Parama Puruśa goes on. Human life attains fulfilment by taking part in that rásaliilá. If this Vaekuńt́ha exists, everything will exist.

points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Where is this Vaekuńt́ha located? Do you know the story of the Vraja bhaktamańd́alii [Hariparimańd́ala devotees], the
summary: Where is this Vaekuńt́ha located? Do you know the story of the Vraja bhaktamańd́alii [Hariparimańd́ala devotees], the simple and naive gopiis? Once Lord Krś
points.body: Where is this Vaekuńt́ha located? Do you know the story of the Vraja bhaktamańd́alii [Hariparimańd́ala devotees], the simple and naive gopiis? Once Lord Krśńa feigned illness. No medicine could heal Him. Worried, Narada asked Krśńa, “Lord, please tell me which medicine can cure you.” Krśńa replied, “Look, Narada, if you can bring the dust from the feet of a devotee, then my headache will be cured.”

points.title: Narada went everywhere in search of the dust from the feet of a devotee. But wherever he w

points.body: Narada went everywhere in search of the dust from the feet of a devotee. But wherever he went, all, including great devotees, said, “It is a sin just to hear you say that! The Lord is our supreme object of worship. How we can give the dust from our feet to be applied to His head? Such great arrogance would be hard to imagine.”

points.title: Finally, Narada went to the Vraja gopiis. In this context let me tell you one thing. The w

summary: Finally, Narada went to the Vraja gopiis. In this context let me tell you one thing. The word gopa or gopii has been derived from the Sanskrit root verb gop. Th
points.body: Finally, Narada went to the Vraja gopiis. In this context let me tell you one thing. The word gopa or gopii has been derived from the Sanskrit root verb gop. The root verb gop means “to give bliss”. Gopáyate yah sahgopah – that is, “One who gives bliss to Bhagaván is a gop or gopii.” Devotion is nothing but giving bliss to God.

points.title: Anyway, upon hearing Naradaʼs message, the gopiis agreed to give the dust from their feet
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Anyway, upon hearing Naradaʼs message, the gopiis agreed to give the dust from their feet at that very moment. Narada sa
summary: Anyway, upon hearing Naradaʼs message, the gopiis agreed to give the dust from their feet at that very moment. Narada said, “You are giving the dust of your fee
points.body: Anyway, upon hearing Naradaʼs message, the gopiis agreed to give the dust from their feet at that very moment. Narada said, “You are giving the dust of your feet. The Lord will touch it on His forehead. Will you not become sinners?” Without the least hesitation, the gopiis answered, “Great sage, if we become sinners, so be it, but the illness of our Prabhu, our Lord, will be healed. We are ready to bear all sins for our beloved Lord.” This is real devotion. This type of real devoteeʼs heart is the abode of Vishnu.

points.body: In the scriptures and kiirtanas the word Hariparimańd́ala is often mentioned. You know that for a devotee, the dearest entity is Parama Puruśa or Hari as He is the only entity in this universe which lasts for eternity. Parama Puruśa alone remains with humans until the end; all other entities are finite, limited. Only Hari and Harikathá [stories and discussion about Parama Puruśa] are endless. That is why intelligent people should establish a relationship of deep love with the Infinite Entity.

points.title: Hari is an internal entity, residing in the innermost core of everyoneʼs heart. Be it the
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Hari is an internal entity, residing in the innermost core of everyoneʼs heart. Be it the heart of a bird, a fool, a sch
summary: Hari is an internal entity, residing in the innermost core of everyoneʼs heart. Be it the heart of a bird, a fool, a scholar, a good person or a bad person, Har
points.body: Hari is an internal entity, residing in the innermost core of everyoneʼs heart. Be it the heart of a bird, a fool, a scholar, a good person or a bad person, Hariʼs throne is there. He only considers one thing – whether that heart has love and devotion for Him. Suppose a certain person commits so many sins; rather, is totally immersed in the ocean of sin: Hari resides even in such a sinnerʼs heart and will reside there in the future, too. He will examine that heart to see how much love and devotion there is for Him.

points.title: Whenever the devotees of Hari assemble together they do not like to gossip, but prefer to

summary: Whenever the devotees of Hari assemble together they do not like to gossip, but prefer to do Hari kiirtana, and nothing else. Whoever comes within the circumfer
points.body: Whenever the devotees of Hari assemble together they do not like to gossip, but prefer to do Hari kiirtana, and nothing else. Whoever comes within the circumference of that spiritual gathering will certainly feel an irresistible desire to participate in that spiritual dance. The sweet spiritual environment created by the kiirtana is called Hariparimańd́ala in the scriptures. Hari resides at its nucleus.

points.title: Those in the Hariparimańd́ala are by nature devotional. When they participate in the kiir

summary: Those in the Hariparimańd́ala are by nature devotional. When they participate in the kiirtana they become even more devotional. Whenever Hariparimańd́ala is c
points.body: Those in the Hariparimańd́ala are by nature devotional. When they participate in the kiirtana they become even more devotional. Whenever Hariparimańd́ala is created, be it for five minutes, three hours or twenty-four hours, due to the intense collective devotion, the environment becomes so sweet and blissful that it becomes highly congenial for spiritual ideation (dhyána). At that time Hari moves His nucleus there and becomes the focal point of dhyána, the object of ideation.

points.title: From the devotional point of view, it is certainly Hariparimańd́ala, and from Hariʼs poin
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: From the devotional point of view, it is certainly Hariparimańd́ala, and from Hariʼs point of view it is also Hariparim
summary: From the devotional point of view, it is certainly Hariparimańd́ala, and from Hariʼs point of view it is also Hariparimańd́ala. As these two viewpoints coinci
points.body: From the devotional point of view, it is certainly Hariparimańd́ala, and from Hariʼs point of view it is also Hariparimańd́ala. As these two viewpoints coincide at one point, every spiritual aspirant enjoys endless bliss. Thus it is said, Bhaktih bhaktasya jiivanam. Just as a fish cannot live without [water, a human being cannot live without] the earth, and a bird cannot live without the sky, a devotee cannot live without devotion. Without Hari the very existence of a devotee is endangered. If devotees are estranged from Hari, or separated from devotion, they become as miserable as a fish out of water.

points.title: The worst calamity that can befall a devotee is to be separated from devotion. Those who t
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: The worst calamity that can befall a devotee is to be separated from devotion. Those who try to deprive people of devoti
summary: The worst calamity that can befall a devotee is to be separated from devotion. Those who try to deprive people of devotion, who tried in the past, and will try
points.body: The worst calamity that can befall a devotee is to be separated from devotion. Those who try to deprive people of devotion, who tried in the past, and will try in the future, certainly invite their own destruction. Hari never wants to harm anyone, nor do His devotees. However, if an individual or a force tries to disturb the Hariparimańd́ala of the devotee, or will try to do so in the future, they will certainly meet their destruction; it is a natural law. It is not at all necessary to harbour any thought of othersʼ destruction. Destruction comes as a matter of course.

points.title: You know, there is a time-honoured theory of cause and effect. It is a recognized fact, a
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: You know, there is a time-honoured theory of cause and effect. It is a recognized fact, a recognized standard of veracit
summary: You know, there is a time-honoured theory of cause and effect. It is a recognized fact, a recognized standard of veracity, that wherever there is effect there m
points.body: You know, there is a time-honoured theory of cause and effect. It is a recognized fact, a recognized standard of veracity, that wherever there is effect there must be cause. This was propounded by Maharshi Kanada. He first said that where there is an effect there must be a cause. We may or may not know the cause, but the cause is there. At the same time you should remember that wherever there is effect, there must be the cause, but wherever there is cause there may or may not be an effect.

points.title: You see, wherever you find any sprout, the cause is the seed; but wherever there is a seed
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: You see, wherever you find any sprout, the cause is the seed; but wherever there is a seed there may or may not be a spr
summary: You see, wherever you find any sprout, the cause is the seed; but wherever there is a seed there may or may not be a sprout. That seed may lack in qualification
points.body: You see, wherever you find any sprout, the cause is the seed; but wherever there is a seed there may or may not be a sprout. That seed may lack in qualifications for creating a sprout; or the seed may have had the power to create the sprout but did not create it. From a bad seed, from a weak seed, there will not be any sprout – but even if there is a very good seed, but that seed does not come in contact with earth, or air, or water, or light, in that case there will not be any sprout.

points.body: Here we have come. Our coming is the effect of some cause. Because it is the effect, what is the cause? Why have we come here? The theory says that it is not non-causal. Then what is it for?

summary: Wherever there is a movement, wherever there is a flow for a long time, if it does not [receive a fresh impetus], what happens? It loses the acceleration. And f
points.body: Wherever there is a movement, wherever there is a flow for a long time, if it does not [receive a fresh impetus], what happens? It loses the acceleration. And finally, what happens? Retardation starts. In our human society there was want of acceleration from the very start. And now the retardation has also started. Now humanity bleeds. The future is dark. So we have come here to do something. I have come here to do something, and you have also come here to do something. My coming is significant, and your coming is not less significant. We have come with a mission; and our lives, singularly and collectively, are a mission. Not missions – ours is a collective mission. Here we all are one. We have come to do something. And that is the causal factor.

summary: And what will be the effect? The effect will be that the world will realize that humanity is one and indivisible, and no power in heaven or on earth can destroy
points.body: And what will be the effect? The effect will be that the world will realize that humanity is one and indivisible, and no power in heaven or on earth can destroy this glorious humanity. We have come here to save humanity, and we will save humanity.

points.body: Another thing. We have come. Our coming is not non-causal, it is causal. And you see, nobody amongst us, A, B, C, X, Y, Z, is – what did I say? Insignificant. Each and every entity has got many a thing to do, and he or she will do it, and you see, our fates have been very closely associated with one another. This shows that in the past there has been some unity amongst us, some closeness, some proximity amongst us. That is why we have come together. It is not meaningless.

points.body: We must always remember this thing. When a group of good people – that group may be of a thousand, that group may be of a million, that group may also be of many billions – but when that group comes, it comes to do something concrete. And that group is known as Hariparimańd́ala gośt́hi, ( 2 ) because that group moves around [makes a circle round] the Cosmic ideology. So you have come here to form a strong, well-knit Hariparimańd́ala for the coming generation.
