points.body: You will have to remember one thing. You will have to acquire the capacity to endure everything. But you will endure only to accumulate strength. If a person attacks you, you have to apply force to resist the attack. But if you do, your force will be misused as a result. What should you do in that case? To [counter-]attack, you have to apply a certain amount of force. Instead, applying less force, preserve the force used by the attacker. Thereafter, combining your own force with the preserved force, you are to repulse the attacker. Suppose, one has aimed an arrow at you. To resist the strike of the arrow, it is necessary to apply an opposite force. But rather than doing that, catch the arrow by applying a smaller amount of force. Thereafter, apply the arrowʼs force [not the arrow] against the attacker. To do this, you must enhance your tolerance. Because taror iva sahiśńuná – I am saying again, do not tolerate only for the sake of tolerance. Tolerate for the sake of counter-attacking.

To Him, no one is either superior to you or inferior to you. All are equal. Therefore, whenever you will all have time, do His kiirtana collectively. If you do kiirtana, your mind will become pure. The speed of spiritual practice will be accelerated, and you will acquire force.

points.body: Trńád api suniicena. A person should be more humble than a blade of grass. Grass is such an ordinary thing. People walk on grass and the grass endures it. However, that grass contains tremendous life force. Rather, grass has even more life force than human beings. How much strength do animals like cows and elephants get by eating grass! Yet this grass bears the neglect of human beings without showing any reaction. But here it does not say “as tolerant as grass”, but rather that human beings will have to acquire more tolerance than grass.

points.body: Let us suppose someone attacks you. What will you do? Will you grab your rifle and run after them? No. First see how much tolerance you have. Endure it to the extent that you are able. Afterwards, if the matter goes beyond your capacity to bear, then that is another matter.

points.body: Now, when you have proven that you have within you enough capacity to endure, then what will happen? Your courage will increase. You will have faith that a certain amount of strength is stored within you. Then if you tell someone, “leave your sinful ways, take to the path of spirituality, take initiation, do sádhaná,” you will find that your work is accomplished. This will be the case nearly ninety percent of the time. And if your work is not accomplished then other path will open up.

points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Taror iva sahiśńuńa. A very large tree which does not bear fruit is called vanaspati in Sanskrit, and a tree which is
summary: Taror iva sahiśńuńa. A very large tree which does not bear fruit is called vanaspati in Sanskrit, and a tree which is large in size but which also bears frui
points.body: Taror iva sahiśńuńa. A very large tree which does not bear fruit is called vanaspati in Sanskrit, and a tree which is large in size but which also bears fruit is called vrkśa or taru, while those trees which are very beautiful to look at are only called taru. If they are not beautiful to look at then they are called vrkśa. In Sanskrit all plants are called mahiiruha, that is, that which parts the earth and rises up. A small sapling can be called mahiiruha even though it is small in size, although in this case it can be called shishu-mahiiruha [baby mahiiruha].

points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: To be tolerant like a taru means that a human being must be as enduring as a vrkśa or taru, which tolerates so many blo
summary: To be tolerant like a taru means that a human being must be as enduring as a vrkśa or taru, which tolerates so many blows and counterblows. However, this does
points.body: To be tolerant like a taru means that a human being must be as enduring as a vrkśa or taru, which tolerates so many blows and counterblows. However, this does not mean that if a wicked person comes to strike you or kill you that you will bear it without protest. It means that you should test how much strength to endure you have within you, so that a deep belief in yourself will awaken through knowing to what extent you can endure.

points.body: Now it is seen that you do not put your capacity to endure to the test. If something happens you react right away. I will say that instead of doing that, from time to time test how much capacity to endure you have inside you so that your self-confidence will become steadier. Be like a tree, which does not protest even if it is cut or ask water from human beings in the scorching heat of summer, but rather gives flowers to the priests and fruits and shade to travelers without asking those priests or travelers for water.

points.body: Just as a tree serves and benefits everyone by giving shade, fruit, flowers and firewood without asking anything in return, a spiritual aspirant should lead their life with the same kind of noble sense of ethics. But it is interesting to see that there are many people in the society who can be heard saying that they have been doing service to society for many years. Their secret wish is that they might be given a pension or a medal. They hope for a recommendation from the government saying that since I played an important role in the struggle for independence then an independent India should give me a government pension. This kind of secret wish remains hidden in their mind. These kinds of people hope for some government title or government grant in exchange for their service to society, just as a shopkeeper exchanges salt for money. Actually such service is not service at all.

points.body: Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ. Ápani nirabhimánii anye dive mána. People commonly show respect to those people who have achieved an honorable position in society, but here Mahaprabhuʼs statement is: show respect to those neglected people who have no position in society, who are not held in esteem, to whom no one shows respect, those whom no one asks how they are doing. Inquire about how they are doing and help them to become established in society.

points.body: You must have often noticed that when a well-dressed gentleman talks, people address them with terms of respect such as ápani [respectful “you”] or ájiṋe [yes, sir]. But when talking with an ordinary labourer, you address them as tumi or tui [familiar and very familiar “You”]. When the stamp of poverty is visible on the face or in the dress then people use the familiar forms of address like tumi or tui, but when the stamp of affluence is on the face or the dress then people spontaneously speak to that person with respect. In Ananda Marga I address everyone with the familiar form, tumi, as in the English “you” [in the intimate sense].

points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Kiirtaniiyáh sadá Harih. What is kiirtana? When someone vocally sings the praises of God so that others can hear, it i
summary: Kiirtaniiyáh sadá Harih. What is kiirtana? When someone vocally sings the praises of God so that others can hear, it is called kiirtana. When it stays on the
points.body: Kiirtaniiyáh sadá Harih. What is kiirtana? When someone vocally sings the praises of God so that others can hear, it is called kiirtana. When it stays on the lips but is barely audible, then it is called mánasokti. And when it is confined to the lips and does not come out at all, then we call it upáḿshu. When it passes the lips and enters into anotherʼs ear then we call it vácanika. When it is not a whisper but can be heard by distant ears, then that loud utterance is kiirtana. If this song of praise does not reach the ears of others, then we cannot classify it as kiirtana or give it the same respect. Now, when one does kiirtana, that person benefits and the person who hears kiirtana also benefits. People also sing bhajanas [devotional songs] in a loud voice, but for their own satisfaction rather than for the satisfaction of others.

points.title: Bhajana is also vácanika but it is not kiirtana. Kiirtana and bhajana are not the same. K
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Bhajana is also vácanika but it is not kiirtana. Kiirtana and bhajana are not the same. Kiirtanaʼs greatness exceeds th
summary: Bhajana is also vácanika but it is not kiirtana. Kiirtana and bhajana are not the same. Kiirtanaʼs greatness exceeds that of bhajana; it is incomparable. The d
points.body: Bhajana is also vácanika but it is not kiirtana. Kiirtana and bhajana are not the same. Kiirtanaʼs greatness exceeds that of bhajana; it is incomparable. The difference between the two is firstly that bhajana is not heard at as great a distance as kiirtana, and secondly that people sing bhajanas so that they can experience happiness, not so much to give happiness to others. Conversely, the ideation behind kiirtana is that others might also enjoy the same happiness listening to the praises of God that I get by singing the praises of God. This is the fundamental difference between bhajana and kiirtana. For this reason, Mahaprabhu has said kiirttaniyah sadá harih, rather than bhajaniiyah sadá harih. The benefit of kiirtana is that one whose mind is dirty becomes purified and one whose mind is already pure becomes even purer. One whose mind is holy becomes even holier. One whose mind was soiled but is no longer so is vimala, and one where it is not known if there was dirt in his or her mind or not, but at present there is not, is called nirmala.

summary: Now, kiirtana helps everyone. Whose kiirtana? Kiirttaniiyah sadá harih, that is, always do the kiirtana of the Lord. In ancient times people used to do the kii
points.body: Now, kiirtana helps everyone. Whose kiirtana? Kiirttaniiyah sadá harih, that is, always do the kiirtana of the Lord. In ancient times people used to do the kiirtana of the kings and emperors. During the Mughal Era, at the time of Akbar, singing the praises of the emperor became a traditional practice. Dilliishvarah jagadiishvaro vá [“Sing the praise of the emperor of Delhi as well as of God in the same tone”]. But what is gained by doing the kiirtana of this mortal man? Mahaprabhu gave the instruction to do the kiirtana of the Lord, not of the emperor.

points.body: Buddha says: “O mendicant, look and see. Water is entering the boat that you have boarded in the hopes of crossing to the other side of the river. So get rid of that water right away.” Sinca bhikkhu imaḿ návaḿ. If you get rid of the water your boatʼs load will be lightened. Sittá te lahu messyati. A human beingʼs burden grows along with the past, the present and the future. For example, perhaps you are thinking: once you were eating rich, delicious and costly foods such as háluyápuri, murg-mashallam, namkiin poláo – this is all the burden of the past. Similarly, today you will eat this and that, you will wear such and such, afterwards you will go to your friendʼs house and they will ask you about what you are wearing – this is the burden of the present. In the same way, you will earn money in the future by doing business, become rich and gain esteem in the society – this is the burden of the future. Buddha warned his mendicants who were thirsty for liberation: O mendicants, lighten the burden that lies before you.

The priests of today openly hanker after dakśińá [an offering in the form of money or property] even after receiving sidhá [an offering in the form of materials such as rice, vegetables.] So whatever form this burden may take, it has to be shaken off. If a person is to reach the other shore of life, then he has to lessen his lifeʼs burden. But human beings are very weak, so they cling to their burden and do not want to give it up. Even if they know that all these things constitute their lifeʼs burden and there is the fear of their lifeʼs boat sinking due to this burden, even then they do not want to give them up. Even if they know that their son is very wicked, they do not want to disown him. So what will happen then? Who will bear their burden? If Parama Puruśa comes to them and says: O human being, give me your burden, I will bear it for you – even then they are not ready to do so.

points.body: There is a story from Japan in this regard. In Japanese their country is called “Nippon”, in English, “Japan”. Once there was an immense load of wood with an old lady. She was at deathʼs door. She was saying: “I have to carry this load of wood every day. If I die now it will be a good thing. How much of a load can I carry everyday in this way! I can no longer take it”. At that very moment the god of death came to her and said: “Old woman, come along with me. You wonʼt have to carry this heavy load any longer”. That burden had been on the hands of old lady for so long. She thought, how best to carry it? The old lady said: “Lord of Death, it is good that you have come. Please lend me a hand. Please pick up my load and place it on my head.”

points.body: Due to the bonds of obstacles people cannot move ahead. Even if they make efforts to free themselves from these bondages they still do not succeed. The mind does not want to distance itself from those bondages because it gets temporary pleasure from them. A dog cuts its lips chewing on a bone in the cremation ground. Blood flows from them and a little of that blood is swallowed. The dog thinks that this is juice coming from the bone. Much later, when a burning sensation starts coming, then it stops chewing on the bone. The same happens with people. They are not getting juice from the bone but rather blood from their own lips.

points.body: Now, without their permission and without their knowledge, Parama Puruśa steals the burden of peopleʼs accumulated saḿskáras, thus one of his names is “Hari”. If he does not steal them, then these weak and obstinate human beings will never be able to cross over to the other side of lifeʼs river. So Hariʼs duty is to lighten the load of human beings. Hence it is only fitting that people do the kiirtana of Hari, their greatest friend, and not of anyone else.

points.body: “If I set out to do some work, believing it to be just and proper, and if the pandits or the moral crusaders abuse me, then let them. I wonʼt let it sway me.” I donʼt depend on the pandits, because in most cases, though not all, the pandits are lazy, indolent fellows. They cannot work, they lack courage and practical intellect; indeed, they are mostly parasites. Pańd́itáh-vanitáh-latáh, that is, “Pandits, women and creepers need some support with which to grow.” I do not want such a thing, so I do not depend on the pandits. As regards vanitá, or women, our girls are committed to standing on their own feet, and I hope that they will very quickly do so. The conception exists that women are dependent on others. It is my firm conviction that they will disprove this contention.

points.body: The pandits – I have just said that they are lazy, indolent fellows – let them abuse me; it wonʼt sway me. Rather I wonʼt even bother to listen to them. I do not have the time. I wonʼt listen to their abuse for even a moment. And if they praise me I do not have the time to listen to that either. I have work to do. I have a goal to reach. And if, as a result of my work, Lakśmii, the goddess of wealth, comes and remains in my house, then well and good. But if she does not then it does not matter. My Prout philosophy does not support capitalism, so we do not go begging for the grace of Lakśmii. Moreover, the people of today have come to understand what the people of yesteryear did not, that Lakśmii is bound to reside in the houses of sinners. Can anyone get rich without resorting to some sort of thievery? Not at all, which means that youʼll find sin wherever you find Lakśmii. If Lakśmii wants to remain in my house then she is welcome; it makes no difference. If she wants to go, then she can go. I have no objection.

summary: That is the story. A dhármik person does not care for what others say; he or she is not afraid of anyone. Whether Lakśmii stays or goes wherever she likes, it
points.body: That is the story. A dhármik person does not care for what others say; he or she is not afraid of anyone. Whether Lakśmii stays or goes wherever she likes, it does not matter at all. Dharma is with the dhármik. Dharmaḿ rakśati rakśitah. One who protects dharma is also protected by dharma. One who is on the true path does not bother about any other direction; he or she does not even think about it. And they will not leave the path that they have chosen as their lifeʼs ideology for anything. If they have to die today as a result of taking that path, or if they have to die after endless time, let it be. It does not matter. Death will come one day – Játasya hi dhruvormrtyuh. One who is born must surely die, today, tomorrow or the next day, one day or another. To curl up and lie down out of fear that death will come is the epitome of foolishness. Such a person cannot accomplish any great work. One should always remain ready for death. Human beings should always remain ready.

points.body: Dvitiiyaḿ shraddhayá yuktaḿ. I must have shraddhá for the goal in whose direction I am moving. In the Vedic language shrat means “ultimate truth, supreme truth, eternal truth”. In other words, that truth which I recognize as supreme, above which there can be nothing higher, is called shrat, and the movement towards that shrat is shraddhá. Shrat – dhá + anat́ + striyáḿ uṋáp. Dvitiiyaḿ shraddhayá yuktaḿ – I will have to have shraddhá for my goal, for the supreme beatitude, for that in which I am striving to be established. This is the second factor.

points.body: Trtiiyaḿ gurupújanam. What is the third one? Gurupújanam. What does guru mean? In the mundane world, in the psychic world, one cannot accomplish anything as long as the darkness of ignorance remains. In ancient Tantra that darkness of ignorance was called gu, and removing that gu, getting rid of it, defeating it, forcefully removing it, was called guru. One who removes the darkness is guru. One will have to maintain devotion for guru who removes this darkness because guru shows the way. If one does not move according to guruʼs word then one can fall into danger at any moment.

points.body: Trtiiyaḿ gurupújanam. There are also different types of gurus. Among these there are three main categories. The first explains things: “Do this, do not do that.” He explains all these things but afterwards he does not endeavour to find out if one is doing it or not. He gives his teachings, takes some dakśińá [ritual offering] as well, accepts prańám [salutation] and some beaten rice, and it ends there. This is the third-class guru. I would prefer not to use the word “guru” for this third class guru.

points.body: The second-class guru is one who gives his teachings, explains things and tries to see if they are following them correctly, if they are walking the proper path. This is the second class guru. They are recognized as guru.

points.body: The first-class guru is one who gives the teachings, certainly, and keeps track of his disciples as well, but who also lets them know that he will punish them to set them right. This is the first-class guru. How is it? Nigrahánugrahe shakto gururityabhidhiiyate. One who loves very much, who loves with all their heart, but who meets out strict punishment when he sees impropriety or mindless action, is the true guru. Here the shloka is talking about this best class of guru, not the middling or lowest class of guru.

summary: Caturtho samatábhávo. This is the fourth factor, to look on all with equal vision, that is, you will not harbour any inferiority or superiority complex. You a
points.body: Caturtho samatábhávo. This is the fourth factor, to look on all with equal vision, that is, you will not harbour any inferiority or superiority complex. You are neither lesser nor greater than anyone else. When everyone is the progeny of the Supreme Father then no one can be inferior or superior. No one can be low caste or high caste. Not only that – the pandits and the fools are brothers; the rich and the poor are brothers. All are children of the Supreme Father. The person who thinks himself to be superior suffers from a mental disease. And the person who thinks himself to be inferior also suffers from a mental disease. As long as this mental disease exists nothing can be accomplished. Inferiority complex is bad; superiority complex is also bad. Defeatist complex is bad, and escapist complex is also bad. Many people think that if they run away from everything then they can perhaps save themselves. That will not do. One has to take strict care of oneʼs responsibilities. The meaning of this shloka is that one must not harbour any kind of complex. No kind of mental disease should be permitted. People speak high-sounding words but do not put them into action. In the field of action they accept untouchability and caste distinction. They are dangerous people. They are not only dangerous for the society but for themselves as well. They have their feet in two different boats. They can drown at any moment. A person has to remain in one boat. A few days ago in Siliguri I said that a person should be ekabuddhi [single-minded], not anekabuddhi [many-minded].

points.body: There is that well-known story. In a pond there lived many fish. One day the fishermen decided to catch all the fish the following morning. Among the fish there was one who was a great intellectual. His name was Shatabuddhi [Hundred-Minded]. He told his wife: “Let the fishermen come, I have a hundred ways to swim away and save myself from them.” There was another fish whose name was Sahasrabuddhi [Thousand-Minded]. Sahasrabuddhi said: “I have a thousand ways to swim away and save myself.” There was another fish whose name was Ekabuddhi [Single-Minded]. He told his wife: “Look, I have only one mind and that mind is telling me that if the fishermen throw their nets then I wonʼt survive. So let us go to another pond during the night.” They left, and the next morning the fishermen came, threw their nets and caught all the fish in the pond. Then the fish Ekabuddhi told his wife:

points.body: So one will have to be “Ekabuddhi”; one must act with a single mind. This single mind teaches the following, that when all are children of the Supreme Father, then there can be no difference of higher or lower. A certain person may be more learned, society may show him or her more respect, but as a human being society cannot consider that person superior to another. All are children of Parama Puruśa, so one who accepts caste distinctions displeases Parama Puruśa. Parama Puruśa is dissatisfied with their behaviour. They will not get his grace. One who thinks another to be stupid, who hates others, suffers from a mental disease. That person hates a child of the Supreme Father, so they can never get his grace. Similarly, one who is wealthy and thinks others to be less than animals, can also never get his grace. His grace remains far away because that person has not yet proven him or herself to be a human being.

points.body: This all-round restraint is indeed necessary. It will not do to simply eat what you get or do what you desire. When you eat you must consider if it is sentient, mutative or static. While eating you must think carefully as to what influence it will have over your body and your mind. You are not a goat or a camel that you will eat whatever you get. You have to think when you act.

points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Śaśt́haiṋca pramitáháro. There is a Bengali saying: Uno bháte duno val, bhará pet́e rasátal. If one eats less, t

points.body: Śaśt́haiṋca pramitáháro. There is a Bengali saying: Uno bháte duno val, bhará pet́e rasátal. If one eats less, then oneʼs strength increases and one does not fall sick, but if someone overeats, then they fall sick. Here it has been said: pramitáhára. Pramitáhára and parimitáhára are not the same. Parimitáhára means that I have not eaten a lot, nor have I eaten a little. That is called parimitáhár. And pramitáhár means that I have eaten little but I have eaten nourishing food. That is pramitáhára. You have the custom of eating sentient food. If you follow that then you meet the objective of pramitáhára.

Shiva has said that there is no seventh cause, it is true, and while I accept this I am adding one more thing. When you get a little time, do a little kiirtana so that the mind will be purified, which will result in greater spiritual progress.

points.body: Todayʼs topic of discourse is “Spiritual Practice and Layers of the Mind”. Every living being has the right to perform spiritual practice. Every living being is the progeny of Parama Puruśa. Parama Puruśa is the Father of all. For this reason, there should not be any difference of high and low among human beings. I said one thing several times. Those who accept caste discrimination do not accept Parama Puruśa, and those who accept Parama Pitá [the Supreme Father] never accept caste discrimination. One has to move as an integral being. It is not possible to move having one leg in one boat and another leg in another boat. To remain alive, one must move forward. A person has to be in one boat. Either accept Parama Puruśa or accept caste discrimination. One cannot accept both at the same time. A stone bowl is made of stone. It cannot be made of gold. So human beings should move ahead along a single path. Adhere to the Singular Entity. Run after the Singular Entity. Build a relationship of devotion and love with the Singular Entity. This is the rule of the path of spiritual practice.

Why then do you not use all His names?” He has names such as Náráyańa, Rama, and so on. Instead of using all those names, you always sing ‘Rama, Rama.’ I know that Rama is your object of meditation. But other names do have significance.” In reply Hanuman said:

summary: That is, “Philosophically, I know that ‘Shriinátha’ means ‘Náráyańa’ [the shelter of the Operative Principle and of devotion] and ‘Jánakiinátha’ means ‘Ra
points.body: That is, “Philosophically, I know that ‘Shriinátha’ means ‘Náráyańa’ [the shelter of the Operative Principle and of devotion] and ‘Jánakiinátha’ means ‘Rama’. There is no difference between the two. I know quite well that they are one and the same. But I do not want to run after many entities or many names. I want to remain in one boat. To me, there is no one else but Rama in the world. I do not know anyone else. I do not accept anyone else.”

points.body: On the path of spiritual practice one must stick with one entity. The thing is, where there is a divisive mentality, one has to remain far away from it. One has to create a relationship of love with the unbroken, immortal Parama Puruśa. To catch Him, one has to rush towards Him. Parama Puruśa may not want you. But you will not give Him up. If Parama Puruśa tells you, “You are a fool, worthless. I donʼt love you,” you will say, “O Parama Puruśa, yes, it is true. I am mean, worthless. But I am Yours alone. Whether you want me or not, I will keep loving You.” A devotee or spiritual aspirant has this single path.

summary: The level of oneʼs sádhaná depends on the psychic level, or psychic layer, [one has attained]. For instance, in the living world, some beings have a bit of ka
points.body: The level of oneʼs sádhaná depends on the psychic level, or psychic layer, [one has attained]. For instance, in the living world, some beings have a bit of kámamaya kośa, and not more than that. Plants understand hunger, thirst, happiness and sorrow, but not more than that. The minds of other animals and plants are a little developed. Animals and birds understand who cares for them and who does not care for them. That is, it is not the case that they understand eating only. They have within themselves a little more than that. They have a little more than that, meaning that these birds and animals understand that Parama Puruśa exists. But they do not have in them the knowledge of what should be done to attain Him. They do not have the knowledge that something must be done to attain Him. This is the difference between humans, and birds and animals. Humans possess a developed mind. Human beings know that they have been sent by Parama Puruśa, that they have come from Parama Puruśa. So their abode is Parama Puruśa. The abode of all living beings is Rama.

points.body: But the psychic levels of all humans are not the same. True, human beings are more developed than animals and birds. But the mental realities of all human beings are not the same. Some see Parama Puruśa in all worldly deeds whereas some do not. They see Parama Puruśa when they do meditation and sing bhajanas [devotional songs] in solitude. Again, there are many people in this world who do not, in the spiritual sphere, see Parama Puruśa in any action. They think, “O Parama Puruśa, if You really exist, please appear before me.” They consider the material world to be everything.

points.title: In the primordial stage all living beings are just like animals. Spiritual awakening takes
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: In the primordial stage all living beings are just like animals. Spiritual awakening takes place when a personʼs proper
summary: In the primordial stage all living beings are just like animals. Spiritual awakening takes place when a personʼs proper spiritual education is completed. Withou
points.body: In the primordial stage all living beings are just like animals. Spiritual awakening takes place when a personʼs proper spiritual education is completed. Without proper spiritual education, without good company, a person remains like an animal. When spiritual yearning arises in the mind of a human being, then that person becomes spiritually hungry, the person feels that something good should be done. “I am surely being showered with the grace of Parama Puruśa. Since I have got a human body by His grace, I must do something.” When this realization dawns on a human being, he/she no longer remains like an animal. At this stage, the person is called viira. Viira means a courageous person. That is, the person is moving forward, boldly fighting against worldly and mental obstacles. One who has in him/her this fighting boldness is a viira. That is, the spiritual path is the path of a viira, not of a coward. This is the second layer.

points.title: The spirit of a viira is, “I shall move forward, boldly fighting against obstacles; I shal

summary: The spirit of a viira is, “I shall move forward, boldly fighting against obstacles; I shall not fear any type of obstacle.” When this feeling takes strong root
points.body: The spirit of a viira is, “I shall move forward, boldly fighting against obstacles; I shall not fear any type of obstacle.” When this feeling takes strong root within the mind, the person will be called a devatá. ( 2 ) In this very human body, the person will become a devatá. In the initial stage, that is, in the animal stage, human beings have in them different kinds of defects. And they try to rectify those defects. This effort, this careful advancement, is their great feat, their superiority. They are superior to animals. Animals do not try to become good, but humans do try. Although there are defects in their conduct, they try their best to become good. This is called Pashvácára Tantra. I have called this pashvácára. [Pashu = “animal”.] Suppose a person is an M.A., has become a pandit. This does not mean that the person has become great. An uneducated person can become great, while a pandit may be small. Here Parama Puruśa does not judge in accordance with learning or intellect. He makes His judgement considering how much prema [divine love] one has in him/her. Those pashvácáriis who are prema sádhakas are certainly the beloved of Parama Puruśa, because they are the progeny of Parama Puruśa, they have been created by Parama Puruśa.

points.body: Scriptures say that because of these pashvácárii sádhakas, Parama Puruśa [must be] Pashupati [Lord of Animals]. “O Parama Puruśa, I am equal to a pashu [an animal]. But I am not far from You. I am a pashu and You are Pashupati.”

summary: As human beings keep on performing spiritual practice, devotional love for Parama Puruśa gradually increases; courage awakens in them; and they get the force t
points.body: As human beings keep on performing spiritual practice, devotional love for Parama Puruśa gradually increases; courage awakens in them; and they get the force to fight against obstacles. They already have force within them, but at that time they also feel that they have force within them. At this stage, they are called viirácárii. The spirit of a viirácárii is “O Parama Puruśa, I am viira [valorous]. I have courage in me. But I got this courage from You. I am a viira and You are Viireshvara [Lord of the Valorous].”.

points.body: There are more rules and regulations at this second stage of spiritual practice. When you are at the stage of being like an animal, I will say, try to take less mutative food, and try to altogether give up static food.

summary: For the stage of viiracariis, I will say, altogether give up static food, and try to altogether give up mutative food. Try to follow discipline more and more. B
points.body: For the stage of viiracariis, I will say, altogether give up static food, and try to altogether give up mutative food. Try to follow discipline more and more. Be strict in following Sixteen Points. I will say all this. But at the same time, I will say that there are no rules during an emergency. If your life is in danger, you can take static food to keep alive. The Sixteen Points can be relaxed to save yourself from enemies, to keep alive. I will say all this. That is, for them [viiracariis], rules are harder than for pashvácáriis.

points.title: For those who are sincere spiritual aspirants, there is no relaxation in the rules and reg
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: For those who are sincere spiritual aspirants, there is no relaxation in the rules and regulations. What is good for the
summary: For those who are sincere spiritual aspirants, there is no relaxation in the rules and regulations. What is good for them? “I absolutely will not take static fo
points.body: For those who are sincere spiritual aspirants, there is no relaxation in the rules and regulations. What is good for them? “I absolutely will not take static food, and will avoid mutative food to the extent possible. I will take only sentient food. I will do spiritual practice in accordance with prescribed rules. I must be strict in following Sixteen Points. Even if my life is in danger, I cannot accept relaxation in following rules and regulations – I will not accept it.” This hard vow is called divyácára – Krameńa devatá bhavet. [Viirabhávaḿ sadá prápya krameńa devatá bhavet – “And when he is firmly established in viirabháva, he becomes a devatá.”]

points.title: While moving along the spiritual path, a pashvácárii sádhaka will learn the practices,
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: While moving along the spiritual path, a pashvácárii sádhaka will learn the practices, will learn concentration. Kiir
summary: While moving along the spiritual path, a pashvácárii sádhaka will learn the practices, will learn concentration. Kiirtana and bhajanas [devotional songs] are
points.body: While moving along the spiritual path, a pashvácárii sádhaka will learn the practices, will learn concentration. Kiirtana and bhajanas [devotional songs] are a must for all sádhakas, so they must certainly practise them. At some point in time the person will become strict in following the rules and regulations, and then the person will learn spiritual practices of a subtle stage, and then will move forward quite easily, because of the inner force that has come. As the person has kept moving forward following rules and regulations, with sentient ideation, his/her force has increased. So along the path of sádhaná, the person will learn spiritual practices of still subtler layers/stages. In accordance with the personʼs psychic layer, the person will, in the sphere of sádhaná, attain that same stage. When the person will arrive at divyácára, he/she will, in the sphere of sádhaná, learn subtler layers/stages of spiritual practice; and will be strict in following rules and regulations; and when the person will do sádhaná and sing bhajanas and kiirtana, he/she will feel that Paramátmá is seated inside him/her. That is, Paramátmá will be with him/her under all circumstances. The person will take His name not only during emergencies; he/she will take His name also in suffering and in pleasure; if the person is in heaven, he/she will take His name, and if the person is in hell, he/she will take His name. If the will of God forces him/her into hell, he/she will not be sorrowful. This is because Paramátmá will go even to hell to build a relationship of love with him/her.

points.title: The only dharma [characteristic] of the life of a true devotee is to remain with Parama Pu

summary: The only dharma [characteristic] of the life of a true devotee is to remain with Parama Puruśa, to set up a relationship of prema [divine love] with Him. He is
points.body: The only dharma [characteristic] of the life of a true devotee is to remain with Parama Puruśa, to set up a relationship of prema [divine love] with Him. He is to be loved to such an extent that, continuing always to love, the person will feel as if he/she has become lost in Him. Thus in the course of spiritual practice in accordance with the particular psychic layer, the teachings of that spiritual layer will be conferred. But, finally, it is to be accepted that the fundamental hub of sádhaná, and its fundamental goal, and its fundamental base and its target point – all these are one, that is, Parama Puruśa. There is no scope for a second entity, there is only one entity. You are to work for that One, you are to move towards that One. You must remember one thing: whichever [level of] spiritual practice you may do, everything will go in vain without devotion for Parama Puruśa. All spiritual paths are founded on divine love. In addition, you should remember one more thing: kiirtana makes the mind subtle in a short period of time. For this reason, you must do kiirtana for some time before spiritual practice. points.body: Yogináḿ hrdaye na ca. What are the hearts of yogis like? Yogash cittavrttinirodah [“Yoga is the suspension of all psychic propensities”]. A human beingʼs heart has good propensities. It has love for Paramátmá. It has compassion for the world. It is service-minded for the world. The heart of a yogi is devoid of all these things. There is no expression of the heartʼs natural propensities. It is like a solid rock. If a person does not shed tears, is he/she a human being or like a rock? Society is for human beings, not rocks. So I do not reside in the dry and hard hearts of yogis, and I do not reside in Vaekuńt́ha. Where do I reside? Madbhaktá yatra gáyanti tatra tiśt́hámi Nárada. “Wherever my devotees do kiirtana, I go to that place.” So to attain me, money is not needed. It is very easy to attain me.

summary: You can say that Paramátmá is omnipresent, so how is it possible that He goes only to that place where His devotees sing kiirtana? It is true that Parama Puru
points.body: You can say that Paramátmá is omnipresent, so how is it possible that He goes only to that place where His devotees sing kiirtana? It is true that Parama Puruśa pervades the entire Cosmos. Therefore one of His names is Viśńu. He is all-pervading, immanent in everything, so He is called Viśńu. But this Viśńu works from a particular core centre, a particular nucleus, a particular hub. This nucleus or hub is called Puruśottama, is called Parama Puruśa. Parama Puruśa is the object of meditation of living beings, and their goal. Whatever you do, you do for Him alone. He is Táraka Brahma [Supreme Consciousness in Its liberating aspect]. Wherever you sing kiirtana, Táraka Brahma transfers His nucleus, His hub to that place.

summary: Kiirtana is part and parcel of a spiritual aspirantʼs life. One who ignores or neglects kiirtana moves away from Parama Puruśa even if the person does much spi
points.body: Kiirtana is part and parcel of a spiritual aspirantʼs life. One who ignores or neglects kiirtana moves away from Parama Puruśa even if the person does much spiritual practice. You are spiritual aspirants, you want the company of Parama Puruśa, so under no circumstances should you neglect kiirtana. The more you do kiirtana, the closer your mind will come to Him. Whether or not you have learning, whether or not you have wealth, Parama Puruśa will become your supreme wealth. Shubham astu.

points.body: During Anandanagar Dharmamahácakra I spoke about tritvameká bhakti [three kinds of devotion in one]. The idea that devotion is the treasure of humans alone is wrong. Sámánya bhakti [ordinary devotion, natural devotion], sádhárańa bhakti [general devotion], is there also in developed animals. And one who, through individual effort, through sádhaná, enhances [oneʼs own] ordinary devotion, nourishes it, is alone a human being. This more developed ordinary devotion is called gaońa bhakti [lesser devotion]. Finally, this lesser devotion is converted into mukhya bhakti [eminent devotion]. In addition, that greatness, that inexpressibility attracts everyone. Parama Puruśa’s knowledge and erudition, Parama Puruśa’s all-round prema, ( 1 ) and His parental love for all, cannot but attract. It attracts not only human beings but also animals.

This does not occur in the case of birds and animals. A special type of developed body is needed. That body is called a human body.

points.body: Again, it is said that what should be understood as jiṋána [knowledge] is only átmajiṋána [self-knowledge]. Other kinds of knowledge are not knowledge. They are the garbage of knowledge. It awakens ego. One thinks, I know all this, I know so much. But on the field of action, when one happens to be in an awkward situation, in deep trouble, one says, “Oh my God! In fact, I knew nothing.The feeling of ‘I know,’ ‘I know’ inflated my ego. I have received a hard blow. Now I understand very clearly that I knew nothing. I received this blow due to the ego of knowledge.” This is what happens to human beings.

points.body: And not only that. Physical knowledge has another defect. Sometimes the body does not function, the brain does not work. The human being who studied so much forgets all his or her acquired knowledge. This is the condition of human beings. So knowledge means self-knowledge, knowing oneself. Knowing oneself means knowing Parama Puruśa. Because it is Shiva who is present in the forms of living beings. To know a living being is nothing but to know Shiva. But here the difficulty is that on the one hand, it is said that a living being gets a human body as it moves forward through clash and cohesion. If in that condition [having undergone the clash and cohesion], he/she had not gotten a human body, it would not have been possible for further unfolding of the intellect to occur – it would not have been possible in an animal body. That is why he/she gets a human body.

points.body: However, Shiva says: Sukrtae rmánavo bhutvá jiṋánii cen mokśam ápnuyát. That is, “When, after passing through many animal lives and by doing animalistic good deeds, the total of its good deeds increases, it gets a human body, and it attains Parama Puruśa.”

summary: Now, to an animal, there is no such thing as good deeds and bad deeds. It has no intelligence, no power of judgement. How can they do good actions and bad actio
points.body: Now, to an animal, there is no such thing as good deeds and bad deeds. It has no intelligence, no power of judgement. How can they do good actions and bad actions? Their brains are undeveloped, inferior. Suppose that a little boy of ours does something – a four- or five-year-old boy does something mischievous. We say, “He is a little boy. He knows nothing. How much intellect does he possess! Let us forgive him.” Similar is the case with animals. How can they do good deeds or bad deeds? I just answered this question, and I gave a hint about it at Anandanagar, saying that animals have natural devotion. Because to suddenly become motionless at the sight of greatness, to become overwhelmed by greatness, is not the characteristic of human beings only. Animals have that same characteristic. Suppose a huge fire is blazing somewhere. Seeing it, a human will suddenly become motionless, and an animal also will suddenly become motionless. Regarding this, human beings and anmals are equal. Both human beings and animals have natural devotion. Now, sometimes human beings convert the natural devotion of animals into devotion for their masters. A dog has natural devotion for Parama Puruśa. Human beings use this to domesticate it. They transform the devotion in it into devotion for its master. Not all animals have this trait. Developed animals alone possess this trait. Animals whose minds are quite developed have it.

summary: Animals have natural devotion. So has every developed living being. Through that natural devotion, knowingly or unknowingly, shraddhayá helayá vá [“with reve
points.body: Animals have natural devotion. So has every developed living being. Through that natural devotion, knowingly or unknowingly, shraddhayá helayá vá [“with reverence or with indifference”], it cultivates itself; not knowing about the Great One it cultivates itself; that is, knowing about the Great One or not, it begins to think. That is the result of its good deeds. Knowingly or unknowingly, the thinking process is going on, and as a result, their minds are getting developed. Because of this, the path of getting a human body becomes easy.

summary: There are some beings whose body is like that of a human, but whose buddhi-suddhi [intellect] is not like that of human beings. They have natural devotion. But
points.body: There are some beings whose body is like that of a human, but whose buddhi-suddhi [intellect] is not like that of human beings. They have natural devotion. But they are not, by moving along the puśt́i márga [path of devotion], converting that ordinary devotion into lesser devotion or eminent devotion. They remain caught up in worldly things. Scripture says about them that they are like animals. Just as animals can unknowingly, become great, become human, by thinking about Parama Puruśa, so it is said of that kind of sub-human beings in human bodies that if they think about Parama Puruśa, shraddhayá helayá vá – either with respect or with disrespect, they also get elevated. Those humans may not get mokśa [non-qualified liberation], but they will get developed, there is no doubt about that matter.

points.body: And those who, having gotten a human body, cultivate lesser devotion, or through sádhaná, through effort, convert ordinary devotion into lesser devotion and through sádhaná, sacrifice, and love for God convert lesser devotion into eminent devotion, are extraordinary. They are not ordinary. It would be improper to call them ordinary beings. And the best proof of the fact that they are not ordinary beings is that animals do not know that they are very dear to Parama Puruśa. They do not know that they are the children of Parama Puruśa. They do not know that they are Parama Puruśa’s very own. But a human being knows that he/she is born out of Parama Puruśa, that he/she remains in Parama Puruśa, and that the lap of Parama Puruśa is his/her final desideratum. So he/she knows that he/she is very much Parama Puruśa’s own. Parama Puruśa is not a far-away thing. Parama Puruśa doesnʼt hear [only] the words that he/she speaks, He hears the words in his/her mind. Devotees have this buddhi [intelligence]. So devotees are not ordinary human beings. Náráyańa says, “Devotees are superior to me.” Why? Because, if He had no devotees, who would have preached His glory? That is why devotees are given so much importance. Náráyańa resides in the hearts of devotees because their hearts are filled with devotion. in their hearts there is no wickedness, there is no crookedness, there is no hypocrisy. So He says, Madbhaktá yatra gáyanti tatra tiśt́hámi Nárada.

summary: He says, “I am not located in Golokadháma nor am I located in Vaekuńt́ha. Wherever my devotees think of me with all their hearts, speak about me, I go and arr
points.body: He says, “I am not located in Golokadháma nor am I located in Vaekuńt́ha. Wherever my devotees think of me with all their hearts, speak about me, I go and arrive there”. I told you one thing at Anandanagar. You will go near to God through spiritual practice. And you will attract God near you through bhajanas [devotional songs] and kiirtana. So it is the rule to do kiirtana before sitting for spiritual practice. By doing kiirtana, you will draw Him somewhat near to you to. Then you can move a little further towards Him through spiritual practice. For this reason, devotional scripture sings the glory of kiirtana. It says one thing: they alone will do kiirtana who are knowingly getting close to Parama Puruśa and drawing Him near them.

In the ancient world there was no custom of writing itihása. A chronology of of some incident is called itikathá [factual history]: “The king came, conquered a country and died.” This is itikathá – history. What educative value does it have? If there is anything worth learning from, it is named itihása.

summary: The history of India is replete with great human beings named Shankara. They influenced people in different ways. One of them was Adi Shankaracharya. He was bor
points.body: The history of India is replete with great human beings named Shankara. They influenced people in different ways. One of them was Adi Shankaracharya. He was born in Kaladi, in Kerala. He was the propounder of Advaetaváda, and particularly a preacher of máyaváda. He established four monasteries in the four corners of India. His aim was to make the foundation of Paoráńika Dharma [the Puranic cult or religion] strong. The four monasteries are Joshii Math [monastery], Shrngerii Math, Govardhan Math and Shárada Math.

points.body: Anyway, for all these reasons, people generally did not have the desire to write itihása. There were two exceptions. They are the Rájatarauṋginii, penned by Kalhana, which contains the itihása of Kashmir, and the Rájamálá, about Tripura. The Rájamálá and Rájatarauṋginii are written in Bengali and Sanskrit, respectively. But in the Rájamálá and the Rájatarauṋginii, to the extent that the writers praised the king and his clan, they did not venture anywhere near the truth.

points.body: Thakur Krishnadas Kaviraj, biographer and historian, first wrote [true] history, about the life of Mahaprabhu. He (Kaviraj) was born in Jhamatpur Village, which falls within the Ketugram Police Station, in the Katwa Sub-Division of Bardhaman (Burdwan) District. So ego must be avoided. It is said that Náráyańa is Darpaharii [Killer of Vanity], he cannot tolerate anyoneʼs vanity. He does not even tolerate the ego of one who is very dear to Him.

summary: Human beings have two complexes. Some suffer from inferiority complex, while others suffer from superiority complex. Both complexes are bad. One who has an infe
points.body: Human beings have two complexes. Some suffer from inferiority complex, while others suffer from superiority complex. Both complexes are bad. One who has an inferiority complex does not have the courage to come to Parama Puruśa in the realm of ideation. The person thinks, “He is so great, I am so small. How can I have the confidence to go near Him!” One who has a superiority complex thinks, “Am I inferior?” The moment the person thinks like that, his/her progress comes to an end. So what should a human being do? The person should not give indulgence to an inferiority complex. Again, in the case of superiority complex, se buno olt́á bághá teṋtul diye niut́ryáláij karte hay [it has to be dealt with just as the unpalatable effect of wild yam is neutralized by applying extremely sour tamarind]. That is, whenever ego arises, one has to think, “What do I possess to be egotistical about? Learning and intelligence are temporary things. But yes, I do have one thing to be egotistical about. ‘Parama Puruśa is mine.’ This is my pride.” With that pride, he/she will smash the remaining worldly prides to smithereens. This is the significance of Trńád api suniicena [“more humble even than the grass”]. If ego awakens, it is to be struck with a hammer.

In order to see him/her, one has to look towards the sky. How big that person is! Everyone fears him/her. That is, all of peopleʼs ego and vanity come to an end. People surrender themselves to his/her greatness. So, what is being said? Taror iva sahiśńuná [“as tolerant as the trees”].

points.body: Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ [“Giving respect to those whom no one respects”]. In this world, everybody respects people who possess a lot of something. But if someone does not have the honour of possession, the ornament of possession, they will be disregarded by all. Suppose, a person is meticulously dressed. People will tell that person, “Oh, Dádá [elder brother], will you kindly listen to my story?” Then take a poor human being who may be educated, and may have many qualities, but who appears to be poor. People will address him/her like this: “Oh, poor fellow! Come and listen to me.” What is this kind of talk? “Will you kindly listen to me” becomes “Come and listen to me!” Give honour to those who are not given honour. If you honour them, you will make psychic progress. You will have mental calmness. By giving honour to that Náráyańa in the form of a poor person, you will honour yourself. That is, only then will you realize the real company and touch of Náráyańa. Otherwise, everything will become hazy with the smoke of ego.

points.body: Kiirtaniyah sadá Harih [“Always do kiirtana to the Lord”]. A funny thing happens. A person will either praise himself/herself, or will try to hear others praising him/her. He/she will do either of those two. That is the rule. But what will he/she do where there is no opportunity for either? Where there is no opportunity to do either of those two, he/she will condemn others to try to alleviate his/her hunger [for praise]. This is the nature of human beings. For three bad features of human nature – singing oneʼs own praises more and more, trying to get others to praise oneself, and condemning others – the way to save oneself from these mental diseases is to do kiirtana at the top of oneʼs voice. If you do kiirtana, no such disease will get the chance to enter into you. None of them will get the opportunity to infect you.

Usually the word tantra is derived from tan plus trae plus d́a. The root verb tan means “to expand”. The process by which one attains liberation from all bondages by strengthening and expanding oneʼs entitative existence is called Tantra.

points.body: The word tantra can be interpreted in yet another way. Each and every entity, each and every existence, has an acoustic expression of its own. For instance, ta is the acoustic root of dullness or inertness. And the process that brings liberation from this state of staticity, or ta, is called “Tantra”. Taḿ jád́yát tárayet yastu sah tantrah parikiirtitah [“That which redeems human beings and paves the way for their emancipation from the bondages of staticity is called Tantra.”]

points.body: Mayyeva sakalaḿ játam [“All created beings have evolved out of Me”]. The word játam is derived from the root jan plus the suffix kta. Here the Cognitive Entity has been recognized as the primordial cause of creation. Obviously, this is a major difference between Tantra and the Sáḿkhya school of philosophy, for in Sáḿkhya, Prakrti [the Supreme Operative Principle] has been given the dominant role. But in Tantra, Parama Puruśa [Supreme Entity] has been given the dominant role. Ánanda Sútram ( 2 ) clearly states, Shaktih Sá Shivasya Shaktih. Shakti [Prakrti], the Supreme Operative Principle, carries on Her creative flow according to the expressed desire or expressed approval of Parama Puruśa. Hence Puruśa is the prime cause of creation.

points.title: Mayyeva sakalaḿ játaḿ Mayi sarvaḿ pratiśt́hitam. Since everything in this universe is
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Mayyeva sakalaḿ játaḿ Mayi sarvaḿ pratiśt́hitam. Since everything in this universe is born out of Puruśa [Consciou
summary: Mayyeva sakalaḿ játaḿ Mayi sarvaḿ pratiśt́hitam. Since everything in this universe is born out of Puruśa [Consciousness], there is nothing beyond or outsi
points.body: Mayyeva sakalaḿ játaḿ Mayi sarvaḿ pratiśt́hitam. Since everything in this universe is born out of Puruśa [Consciousness], there is nothing beyond or outside Puruśa; hence Mayi sarvaḿ pratiśt́hitam – “everything is residing in Him.” He is the base of everything; there is no way to go beyond Him. Human beings may go a little way from Puruśottama, the Supreme Nucleus of the universe; they may increase the length of their radius; but they can never go beyond the Cosmic periphery. In fact, every object emerging from Him in the phase of saiṋcara is maintained in Him, and in the phase of pratisaiṋcara ( 3 ) is finally dissolved in Him. That is to say, the Entity who was in the beginning and the middle, is also present in the end.

To say that Prakrti [Cosmic Operative Principle] is doing everything, one will have to admit that Nature is everything, but basically Nature is a blind force; she cannot do anything by herself unless supported by intellect.

points.body: As mentioned earlier, in Tantra, sádhaná has been given the utmost importance. What is sádhaná? Sádhaná means practical effort. An effort to what? An endless effort to move towards Puruśottama, the Nucleus of the Cosmic Cycle.

summary: Now, this movement from imperfection to perfection, and in fact every movement in this universe, is not without obstacles. Fundamentally every movement involves
points.body: Now, this movement from imperfection to perfection, and in fact every movement in this universe, is not without obstacles. Fundamentally every movement involves opposition, and the resultant achieved during the fight against the obstacles is called progress. So the more vigorously one tries to move towards the goal, the more vehemently one will to have fight against obstacles. Those who are averse to struggle will never make any progress; what to speak of progress, without struggle one will lag behind. Hence, struggle is the essence of life. Those who abhor struggle, who consider struggle to be violence, have no place in this universe. Not only that, they are hypocrites, for although in practical life they have to resort to struggle, outwardly they hesitate to confess it. They feel that if they admit it openly they will become debased in public estimation. They fail to realize that by denying the plain truth, they are hurting themselves [by acting against their own consciences].

points.body: This cult of Tantra, as enunciated by Shiva, was the first to show human beings how to attain Brahma. The earlier methods of incantation, contemplation, eulogy, or repetition of hymns, attempted in various ways to lead human beings towards Brahma, but to no avail. The essential thing is to come in the closest proximity to Parama Puruśa, to be established in Brahma. That is why Tantra proclaims:

It is said, Yádrshii bhávaná yasya siddhirbhavati tádrshii [“As you think, so you become”]. The aspirantsʼ own entitative existence will be turned into clay, metal or wood – a state which in the scriptures is called Prakrtiliina. It is a dreadful state.

points.body: Higher than idol worship is the practice of dhárańá [spiritual concentration] and dhyána [to assimilate totally the entire inferences being emanated from the Iśt́a, or Beloved Goal, with deep devotion and an acute intensity of love for Him], through which one can make steady progress. The last stage is called nirvikalpa samádhi [trance of indeterminate absorption in Consciousness], or asamprajiṋáta [beyond all cognition] samádhi, which is otherwise known as uttamá sahajávasthá [highest natural state], or, in the language of other scriptures, uttamo Brahmasadbhávah [realization of the highest stance of the Supreme].

points.body: Many may think that since Tantra is a rigorous practice, a hard reality, then in Tantra there must not be any scope for sweet kiirtana. But certainly there is scope for kiirtana. Tantra exhorts spiritual aspirants to advance towards their goal, smashing the boulders of obstacles and impediments; it never tells people to suppress their sweet sentiments. On the contrary, it advises spiritual aspirants that the more love and devotion they develop for the Cosmic Goal, the more speedily they move towards Him. Hence Tantra recognizes all kinds of sweet sentiments. Kiirtana, song, dance, instrumental music – all are accepted in Tantra and unambiguously recognized as vehicles to ensure spiritual progress.

points.body: And what is more, Sadáshiva Himself was the original propounder of song, dance and instrumental music. Tantra is based on reality, and takes the qualities of the Supreme Entity in a practical way. In Tantra, Shiva is not an imaginary entity; rather He has been accepted as the benevolent Father. That is why even today, in the society of devotees, Shivaʼs popularity remains totally unimpaired, because He is the original father of Tantra.

summary: As He is feared by all, every action in this universe is being properly undertaken. Were He not apparently dreadful, He would not be able to discharge His respo
points.body: As He is feared by all, every action in this universe is being properly undertaken. Were He not apparently dreadful, He would not be able to discharge His responsibilities properly. Tantra has made such a realistic appraisal of Parama Puruśa and said: Bhiiśasmádváyuh pavate – “The wind blows on time out of fear of Him; it never completely ceases to blow under any circumstances” . . . bhiiśoʼdeti súryah – “out of fear of Him, the sun rises on time every day without the least deviation” . . . bhiiśasmádagnishcendrashca mrtyuh dhávati paiṋcamah tasmáducyate bhiiśańamiti – “out of fear of Him, fire burns, and Indra faithfully discharges his duty” (“Indra” means “energy”; due to fear of Parama Puruśa, all other energies are doing their duties according to their inherent characteristics) “and due to fear of Him, death reaches the proper person at the proper time.” Death cannot say that he will reach somebody a couple of days later. Out of fear, he will always arrive at the stipulated time.

points.title: Gatih práńinám [“You are the very movement of all living entities”]. The property of mo
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Gatih práńinám [“You are the very movement of all living entities”]. The property of movement, of dynamism, is one of
summary: Gatih práńinám [“You are the very movement of all living entities”]. The property of movement, of dynamism, is one of the basic characteristics of our Suprem
points.body: Gatih práńinám [“You are the very movement of all living entities”]. The property of movement, of dynamism, is one of the basic characteristics of our Supreme Lord. Life also is characterized by movement. We distinguish between living and non-living entities on the basis of their movement. Those who lack in dynamism, though physically they may be alive, are virtually dead: there is no justification for their existence. Hence my exhortation to all is to become active, vigorously active. This quality of dynamism comes directly from Parama Puruśa, because He Himself is always dynamic.

points.title: Pávanaḿ pávanánám. Human beings consider certain objects to be sacred; those objects

summary: Pávanaḿ pávanánám. Human beings consider certain objects to be sacred; those objects are called pávana in Sanskrit. “And those sacred objects in turn look
points.body: Pávanaḿ pávanánám. Human beings consider certain objects to be sacred; those objects are called pávana in Sanskrit. “And those sacred objects in turn look upon Parama Puruśa as sacred.” Indeed, they themselves are considered sacred because they are related to Him, otherwise they would not be sacred.

points.title: Mahoccaeh padánáḿ niyantr tadekam. In this world various persons occupy various exalted
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Mahoccaeh padánáḿ niyantr tadekam. In this world various persons occupy various exalted posts, and because of their p
summary: Mahoccaeh padánáḿ niyantr tadekam. In this world various persons occupy various exalted posts, and because of their posts they enjoy social respect and posit
points.body: Mahoccaeh padánáḿ niyantr tadekam. In this world various persons occupy various exalted posts, and because of their posts they enjoy social respect and position. “But however high their rank may be, they pray to the Lord, saying, ‘O Lord, I exist by Your Grace – protect me, O Lord.’” So the Lord is controlling everyone, whatever may be their post. The moment one transgresses oneʼs jurisdiction out of vanity or ego, one is removed from that post. Whenever one misuses or abuses oneʼs authority, the Lord pushes the person out, and the person falls on his knees. This is the rule. The Lord is controlling everything; He does not tolerate the abuse of power or authority by anyone. In fact, one of His names is Darpahárii [Stealer of Vanity]. He does not tolerate anyoneʼs darpa [vanity]. We see in practical life that people may be seated today in the most exalted position in society, but if they grossly abuse their position, they will meet with such a great fall that their bones and skin will be altogether beyond recognition.

points.title: Paresháḿ param. In the absence of a witnessing entity, the existence of any entity or ph
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Paresháḿ param. In the absence of a witnessing entity, the existence of any entity or phenomenon cannot be substantiat
summary: Paresháḿ param. In the absence of a witnessing entity, the existence of any entity or phenomenon cannot be substantiated. When an action takes place, there sh
points.body: Paresháḿ param. In the absence of a witnessing entity, the existence of any entity or phenomenon cannot be substantiated. When an action takes place, there should be an entity to witness it, to appreciate it. Due to the presence of the witnessing entity, an action or an object is substantiated. The entity which witnesses is called para, and the entity or entities which are witnessed are called apara. We consider many entities as para or witnessing entities, but “above all these witnessing entities there is one Supreme Witnessing Entity, Parama Puruśa.” Hence He is rightly called Paresháḿ param [“Witness of all witnesses”].

points.title: Rakśakaḿ rakśakánám. In various spheres of life, we look upon various objects or pers
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Rakśakaḿ rakśakánám. In various spheres of life, we look upon various objects or persons as our saviours or protect
summary: Rakśakaḿ rakśakánám. In various spheres of life, we look upon various objects or persons as our saviours or protectors. But “those very persons whom we loo
points.body: Rakśakaḿ rakśakánám. In various spheres of life, we look upon various objects or persons as our saviours or protectors. But “those very persons whom we looked up to as our saviours or protectors, themselves look to Parama Puruśa for protection.” However cautious one might be, there can never be any absolute security for anyone without the protection of Parama Puruśa. No one can say with any certainty that a particular medicine will cure a particular disease. Even the physician who specializes in the treatment of that disease may himself die of that disease. People invent a particular weapon, thinking that it will counteract other weapons; but often it fails. And people are often over-cautious. There is an old saying in Bengali, Sábdháner mára nei, which means, “Caution circumvents trouble;” but Rabindranath Tagore once said that caution no doubt circumvents trouble, but it is also true that trouble sometimes circumvents caution! Hence Tantra teaches that the human mind should be channelized in only one direction, not in a thousand directions.

You, the Supreme Lord, the one without shelter, are the Supreme Culminating Point of all the created beings in the universe.]

points.body: “If anyoneʼs name is to be chanted in japa, it is the name of Parama Puruśa.” What is “japa”? A word has a particular meaning; repeating the word inwardly again and again, after having understood its meaning, is what is termed japa. As a result of the prolonged repetition of a word, whose inner meaning is clearly understood, its ideation becomes permanently imprinted on oneʼs mind, and consequently there occurs a radical change in oneʼs mental arena. The extroversial tendencies of the mind gradually become introverted. This is the benefit of japa. And if anyoneʼs name is to be repeated, it is the name of the Lord.

points.body: Tamekaḿ smarámah. “If one has to take refuge in any entity, or has to contemplate any entity, one should take refuge in or think about only the Supreme One,” because whenever the mind broods on a second entity, it will become one with the latter; that is, if the mind constantly reflects on physicality, oneʼs whole psycho-spiritual existence will become physical. That is a terrible situation.

summary: Tamekaḿ jagatsákśiirúpaḿ namámah. “If there is anyone to whom spiritual aspirants should surrender, if there is anyone to whom they should pay salutations
points.body: Tamekaḿ jagatsákśiirúpaḿ namámah. “If there is anyone to whom spiritual aspirants should surrender, if there is anyone to whom they should pay salutations, it is Parama Puruśa.” The system behind salutations is to look for the Supreme Being that is the inner essence of a person, and to pay salutations to that Parama Puruśa. The generally-accepted rule is that one should say namaskára to a human being or a god or goddess, but one should say namaste or namastubhyam only to Parama Puruśa, not to any other entity.

points.body: Tadekaḿ nidhánam. Human beings run along many different paths, but “ultimately they will have to take the path towards the Supreme One.” Nányapanthá vidyate ayanáyá – “There is no other way for them.” So if they begin in time to run towards the Supreme One, it saves them a lot of time and energy later.

summary: Nirálambamiisham. In this world each and every object requires a support, a strong base. Nothing can maintain its existence without a dependable base. For exam
points.body: Nirálambamiisham. In this world each and every object requires a support, a strong base. Nothing can maintain its existence without a dependable base. For example, the base of Calcutta is West Bengal; and the base of West Bengal is India. The continent of Asia is the base of India, and the base of Asia is our planet earth. The base of the earth is the solar system, and the base of the solar system is Parama Puruśa. But “Parama Puruśa does not depend for His existence upon any base. Rather everything is sheltered in Him – He is the base of everything.” So if human beings have to look for any shelter, it must be a self-supporting, self-sheltered entity.

points.body: Bhavámbodhipotaḿ sharańaḿ vrajámah [“seek shelter on the ship floating on this ocean of bhava”]. “Casting aside all futile arguments and time-consuming propensities of mind, we will seek shelter only in You.”

summary: Bhavámbodhipotam [“ship floating on the ocean of bhava”]. The unrequited saḿskáras [i.e., the as-yet-unserved balance of reactions to oneʼs original actions]
points.body: Bhavámbodhipotam [“ship floating on the ocean of bhava”]. The unrequited saḿskáras [i.e., the as-yet-unserved balance of reactions to oneʼs original actions] which are responsible for oneʼs rebirth are called bhava, and dharma is the means to cross the vast ocean of bhava. To cross this bhava is part of your sádhaná, and is also your dharma. But individually human beings are very weak; it is next to impossible for them to cross the ocean of bhava without the direct help of Parama Puruśa. Máyá ( 4 ) is very powerful; human beings cannot fight against Her singlehandedly. So one must first seek the shelter of Parama Puruśa and then fight against Her. Máyá gives way to the one who is endowed with divine power from Parama Puruśa because She is, after all, the immanent power of Parama Puruśa. Shaktih Sá Shivasya Shaktih. As Krśńa said,

points.body: Now, to cross an ocean, the passengers need to board a ship. Parama Puruśa comes to human beings as a ship does to pick up passengers. What should we do? We should secure a safe shelter on that ship – sharańaḿ vrajámah. All sádhakas are rushing to that ship which will take them to their proper destination. Human beings have to take refuge in that divine ship; they will have to come rushing, without further delay. They should not and must not waste a single moment.

points.body: As I have said previously, our ideology maintains that no one need be afraid of anything under any circumstances. If anyone does become afraid, it should be understood that he or she is doing something opposed to our ideology. So you should remember that no situation will ever arise in this world which will give you cause for fear.

points.title: It has been said that Parama Puruśa is the fear of fear. That is, fear is as afraid of Pa
